utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. If Your Honours please, I seek to produce into evidence the report prepared by Ms. Ewa Tabeau. It was filed, as you know, last year. I've got four copies with court officials. They're in colour, so you can individually have one copy each to follow the evidence, and one of them can be used as the actual exhibit itself, if that's suitable to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the solemn declaration from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I apologise. I jumped the gun. But that will be my course of action once the witness is sworn in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes. You've already introduced the report. What about the C.V., the curriculum vitae? I see it attached --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Within the report itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I intend to produce the entirety of the report because, of course, I rely on that as evidence of her credentials and expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I just wanted to -- I know that the Chamber is concerned about time and so on. I just wanted to outline to you what I propose to do and see if that's agreeable to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'll hear from the Defence. They received the report as indicated by the Prosecutor and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can confirm that we received that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We don't have any objection to admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P133, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what I propose to do - I know that you're mindful of time and so on - is just to ask the witness to identify major features of the report. That will take me a matter of minutes, and then sit down. If that's suitable to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's all I propose to do. Thank you. And may I ask if the interpreters' booth could inform us whether or not they have a copy of the report because, if not, I have an extra copy here which I can make available. I'm informed by my case manager that they do have copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: One final matter. I understand that the copy that was filed with our motion last year is a colour copy. If it's in court with registry officials now, if it's available now, I wonder if it might be temporarily loaned to the Prosecution, as it's in colour and the copies that we have are in black and white.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it in colour?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If not, we'll make do with the black and white, but if it is available, could we just borrow it for the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I brought the filing into court, and it is in colour. It can be given to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If it could be simply kept here on the Prosecution Bench just for the morning and I'll undertake, of course, to return it once the evidence is finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think that can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, I'd like you to just provide commentary on the major aspects of this report, and I'd like you, please, to first of all tell the Trial Chamber what the major features of the report are, and in particular, what the major subject areas of the report are, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This report is titled Changes in the Ethnic Composition in Bosanski Samac and Odzak, 1991 and 1997. It is a report, as suggested by the title, about the ethnic composition, how it used to be before the conflict started in these municipalities and in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the last year, for which we have excellent data source, the population census, 1991, and we then further compare ethnic composition from the pre-wartime with the ethnic composition in the year 1997. Our major goal is to provide reliable statistics that would allow us for assessment, proper assessment, of the scale of changes, and that would give us a deeper insight into the population that used to live there before and after the conflict. Yes. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In our study, we used two sources, information sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If I may just ask you to pause there. I was going to ask you about that. Of course, you were about to go on and explain the sources, and please do, but when you do so, can you comment on whether or not these are commonly used sources for demographic studies; and secondly, if you can offer any commentary on the reliability of those sources that you used in preparing the report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We used two sources: One is, as I said, the population census from 1991; and the second source is voters register from the elections in 1997. Regarding the census, I can say that it is the best information source that we can have as demographers to describe the population size and structure, by very many different dimensions. Population census covers the whole population living at a particular moment of time in a country. Population census is usually conducted and processed -- data is later processed very carefully. I think that also the census in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991 was conducted quite carefully. As to data processing, I am -- as we all know, the conflict started directly -- almost directly after the year the census took place, so certainly there was not enough time and there was not enough attention to process the data in the usual way. But in my view, the quality of this source is very good, even though there are certain problems, like, for instance, errors in the spelling of names and certain information actually would need to be recorded properly in order to obtain a better picture of the changes of the population. Nevertheless, I believe strongly that this is a very complete and reliable source of information. The second source, voters register, is not a source that we can consider official, not at least a source that can be used for producing official statistics. In no country statistical authorities use this type of sources for producing statistics. But we must remember that it is very difficult to find a source for any country in a similar situation to Bosnia and Herzegovina that would be used to show, almost directly after the conflict, the size of the population, and voters register actually can be used for this purpose. It is a huge data source for the election in 1997, more than 2 million voters registered. It was almost 2 and-a-half million voters who registered to vote in this election. If we realise that the whole population, pre-war population of Bosnia and Herzegovina, had 4.4 million individuals, then we realise that 2 and-a-half million is more than half of the population size. This sample -- this must be seen as a sample, as a part of the population, must be seen as a very large sample, and certainly can be used to make conclusions related to the population size, and this is what we have done. Voters register does not include information about ethnicity. In order to classify, regroup, individuals reported in the voters register by ethnicity, we linked voters register with the population census. "Linked" means simply that individual records describing the same persons were searched in the two collections and connected with each other. And in this case, once a person, the same person, was found in the two sources, we could use information about ethnicity from the census for the person who was reported in the voters register. This is very important what I am saying, because all tables, all figures, presented in our report show ethnic composition obtained from the same definition of ethnicity as reported in the population census in 1991. This is very important part of our methodology, the linking or, in other words, matching records from different sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you: Did you -- what sort of precautions did you take to ensure that this linking process was reliable and safe?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The most reliable way of linking records is using individual identification numbers, the so-called maticni broj, if available, of course, in the sources that are being linked. Luckily, in the census and also in the voters register, the maticni broj is reported. Unfortunately, this is not reported for every single voter registered in the voters register. Approximately 80 per cent, or even more than that, voters have the ID. So it was a very fast procedure in this case. For about 80 per cent of voters, about 2 million individuals for the whole country, we were able to quickly link them with the same records in that census. So in this case it was not difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if I may ask you: The subject-matter of the study, geographic subject-matter of the study, I should say, am I correct in saying that that was essentially the pre-war municipalities of Bosanski Samac and Odzak and following upon the Dayton Agreement, those same two municipalities but which had now been divided into four, namely, Domaljevac Samac, or part of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Samac, the Republika Srpska part of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and as far as Odzak is concerned, the federal part of Odzak and what is now Vukosavlje, Republika Srpska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And can I ask you just to show on the map that you have in your -- or the relevant map that you have from your report, just show Their Honours, please, on the ELMO, the basic geographic areas that we are talking about and the Dayton line, and point out the old municipalities and the four new municipalities that emerged following the Dayton Agreement, please. And you've got the marker there to do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't have coloured map, only black and white, but still I think the map is relatively clear. It is, on the other hand, not a very specific map but just an illustration of how the municipalities looked like and where is the Dayton line. What we see on the map are four municipalities, or two municipalities if we would think of pre-war municipalities. So this is approximately the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac. It consists of two parts, in terms of post-war, post-Dayton municipalities: federal part Domaljevac Samac and Serbian part, Samac. And a similar situation we see for Odzak: This is the pre-war Odzak, and here the federal part of Odzak, and Serbian part, Odzak Vukosavlje. The Dayton line, as we see here, is going approximately like that. In your coloured copy of the report, the Dayton line is marked with red, so it is easy to see how the municipalities had been split by the Dayton Peace Accords. So that's the geography. We actually analysed the four municipalities, post-Dayton municipalities, in our study, instead of two pre-war municipalities. The reason for doing this is that there were huge population movements within the pre-war municipalities, and if you would be looking at the pre-war municipalities, the larger entities, then we wouldn't be able to find what was happening within the municipalities with the population. So this is why. Analysing four municipalities gives us the opportunity of being more specific and just making a more thorough analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for that. Now I'd like to ask you to consider the major findings that you made in your report, and where necessary, can you direct the Chamber's attention to any maps or tables that illustrate the major points. Firstly, can we deal with Bosanski Samac. Did you, in fact, conduct a study of the pre-war population of Bosanski Samac but by looking at the post-Dayton split, namely, Domaljevac Samac and Samac Republika Srpska? If you did, what were your major findings there?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I would like to show you a selection of figures and statistics. All material I will be using during my presentation is part of the report, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. When you do show those materials, could you just tell Their Honours what page of the report they will find that at so they can follow it by looking at their own copy and also make a record of it for the future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. I will first refer to figure 1A, which is included on page 9. This figure shows ethnic composition in Domaljevac Samac, federal part of the pre-war Samac, Bosanski Samac. It is a picture that is actually very clear, and we will not spend much time on discussing it. There are two groups of bars -- excuse me. There are four groups of bars included in my charts. One, first group, shows the fraction of Serbs in the population before and after the war. Here, actually, the fraction was very, very small before and after. Next group shows the same for Muslim population. Next one for Croat population, and the last group of bars shows the fraction of other ethnic groups aggregated, taken altogether. First the bar to the left always -- here, for instance, it's very clear. This bar always is illustrating the pre-war situation, 1991 data, and the bar to the right, the 1997 data. In Domaljevac-Samac, before the war, there were 98 per cent of Croats, and the same fraction of Croats lived there after the war, as we obtained from the voters register.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. So essentially, the north-eastern segment of Bosanski Samac, the pre-war Bosanski Samac, has always had high numbers of Croats living in that area?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This has not changed, had not changed --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- between 1991 and 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. Can you go on to comment about the Samac part of -- Samac Republika Srpska part of the former Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Here the picture is more complex. Before the war, Serbs were the absolute majority, with representative 55 per cent, but there were also Croats living there, 27 per cent before the war, 1991; also 10 per cent of Muslims, and a small per cent, 8 per cent, of other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Just before you continue: This, of course, is the part of Bosanski Samac that includes the actual town itself, the city itself, the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: May I put a question just for clarification? Figure 1A covers the whole municipality of Bosanski Samac, including both the villages and the town of Bosanski Samac, and not only the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May I just look at the transcript? I don't think so, if Your Honour pleases. Well, I think not, if Your Honour pleases. Figure 1A only includes the north-eastern part of Bosanski Samac, of the whole pre-war Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, I think you heard His Honour's question.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Figure 1A, am I correct, only applies to a segment, a portion, of the pre-war Bosanski Samac, the north-eastern segment of the former Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And it essentially is the part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If I might, just for my own sake. So it's the part north-east of the red line on the map on side 2, where we have Grebnice --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right. That's absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: And so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would you please continue with your commentary on the Republika Srpska part of the former Bosanski Samac, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The post-war composition is very much different from what we saw for 1991. This is the fraction of Serbs. It is 92 per cent of the Serbian population that we had identified in the voters register. So the representation of other ethnic groups is very small, 1.7 per cent of Muslims, 1.3 per cent of Croats, and 5 per cent of others. So the change in the ethnic composition is quite dramatic in this municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. So essentially, there were always large numbers of Serbs in that part of Bosanski Samac that is now Samac Republika Srpska, but following the war, that high proportion, 55 per cent, jumped dramatically, and all other groups dropped dramatically.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The result would be, of course, that the population of that part of Bosanski Samac became far more homogenous, far more -- purer, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Please, can you comment on the ethnic composition in the pre-war Bosanski Samac as a whole, please?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Pre-war composition of Bosanski Samac was mixed. There were 45 per cent of Croats living there, 41 per cent of Serbs, and Muslims and other ethnic groups altogether -- each of these, Muslims were represented at 7 per cent and others also at 7 per cent. So, obviously, the pre-war Bosanski Samac, as a whole, in terms of the pre-war definition, had a mixed ethnic composition, with two dominant ethnic groups: Croats and Serbs. But there was no majority ethnic group, majority in the sense that there would be one group which would be represented at more than 50 per cent. So obviously, for the whole municipality, the ethnic composition was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can I ask you to go to your -- the major findings that you made in respect of Odzak, please, and essentially cover the same ground that we had covered, pre- and post-war general breakdown of the population --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- and then post-war breakdown of the population in the two separate parts. And can I also ask you to, before you do that, to again illustrate to the Court the geographic area that we are now looking at and which figure we can find it at.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I am now back with the map of Odzak. This is the pre-war municipality Odzak, divided by the Dayton line into Federal Odzak and Odzak Vukosavlje, belonging to Republika Srpska after the Dayton Peace Accords.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you please now comment on the pre-war distribution of the population and its ethnicity, please, and direct us to the relevant tables.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. The pre-war ethnic composition in Odzak had a Croat majority, 54 per cent of Croats living there, and two considerable minorities. One of them was Muslims and the second one was Serbs. Actually, Serbs were represented at 21 per cent and Muslims at 19 per cent. So we have a situation municipality -- Croat municipality in the sense of absolute majority of Croats living there, and two large minorities, each approximately 20 per cent, mixed ethnic composition. It must be seen like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you comment upon the demographic picture presented post-war in the federal part of what was formerly Odzak?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I'm referring now to figure 3A, which is included at page 18 in the report, figure 3A. This is page 18. And statistics shown in this figure are included in table 11A, the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And so can you comment on the picture that is presented there?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In the Federal Odzak before the war, we observed 75 per cent of Croats, which is a very strong majority of Croats, and 22 per cent of Serbs, and actually, other ethnic groups, like Muslims and others, are only very weakly represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. So please tell me if this is a fair comment: It would seem that the proportion of Serbs living in what is now the federal part of Odzak dropped dramatically, the number of Muslims who went to live there obviously climbed dramatically, and the number of Croats stayed at more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That is very correct. That is the post-war, 1997 situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Later in your report -- later in your report, do you comment on where these people went?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. We tried to trace the fate of those who actually lived in these municipalities in 1991, and we have done this also for this municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you briefly explain to the Chamber how you went about that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We actually looked for place of residence of certain persons who were identified as registered voters. In 1991, on the one hand, and in 1997, on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And just while we're diverging briefly here, could I ask you: Did you form any findings or conclusions as to where that population of Serbs that you can see in the federal part, what is now the federal part of Odzak, where they went?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We have done this also for the Serb population who moved out from this municipality. And if I may refer you to figure 3B, page 19 in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Can you explain that figure to the Chamber and --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- what it illustrates?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Please take a good look at this, only this chart, not all of them, because now we are speaking only of the Serb population who moved out of this municipality. In this figure we show the 1997 voters who used to live in this area in 1991, by their place of residence in 1997. Some of them registered to vote, only very few in this municipality, the same municipality where they lived in 1991, but majority of them registered to vote in other municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Some of the Serbs moved out of the country. We can even say where they moved to: many of them to Serbia, but also some of them to countries in Europe or America and other countries. But this bar is the explanation of how they moved, where they moved to. They just left this area and moved to other places in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. As far as that bar in the middle of the red figure 3B dealing with Serbs, indicating that many of them moved to other municipalities, did you ever conduct a study of which other municipalities they moved to?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We made some maps that are included in the report. For this group, only this group, other municipalities, we can indicate on the map of Bosnia and Herzegovina where we found them, and this is figure 3C, page 20 in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And essentially, what conclusion did you draw as far as the Serbs from that part of Odzak are concerned?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is rather clear from this figure that very many of them moved to Bosanski Samac, the part that is today Republika Srpska, but also to other municipalities in the neighbourhood of Odzak and Samac, and other municipalities in Republika Srpska. They just remained in the part called today Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Now, I apologise for this brief diversion. If we can go back now to your analysis that you were conducting of Odzak itself. And I think we've dealt with the federal part. Can we now deal with the part that is now part of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I'm now showing you figure 4A. This is page 22 in the report. Am I correct, or is it 21?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's page 21.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. Yes. It is a matter of how the text is distributed when printing. I'm sorry. 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We see again information about two ethnic compositions in two years, 1991, 1997. 1991, we see two groups, Muslims and Croats, being two large ethnic groups, 38 per cent each of the whole population in this municipality. No one of these groups is a majority, absolute majority group. Serbs are represented at 19 per cent, others 5 per cent. Again, an example of mixed ethnic composition, with two groups, Muslims and Croats, dominating in this municipality. And a completely different situation in 1997: The groups, dominant ethnic groups from 1991 were completely gone by 1997, and the Serbian population increased up to 93 per cent, and practically it is a very homogeneous ethnic composition, with symbolically represented Croats at 2 per cent and 5 per cent of other ethnic groups. That is exactly the same as in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Of course, they're just figures of the percentage breakdown of the population. It doesn't actually mean that a lot of Serbs actually went there, but it means that of people who are now living there, that is, by far, the dominant group are Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. It is, of course, first of all, the result of the fact, the change in ethnic composition, that other ethnic groups are absent in this municipality. So it is not the absolute numbers that we are discussing here, but relative numbers, fractions, percentages. So the increase is dramatic increase, first of all, the result of the absence of other ethnic groups. But there were certainly newcomers, Serb newcomers, who moved into this municipality from other areas of this region, say, put it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. When we are talking about the relations between different ethnic groups, I think it would be most useful also to have the figures of the total population in that area, because otherwise this is misleading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may answer. Yes? We actually include some figures that say something about the population size, together with the chart that I'm discussing right now, and for this particular municipality, if we look at table 12A, page 22 in my copy -- is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 22, table 12A. Then we see -- this is a very small municipality, and in the first column of statistics, where the census figures are reported, we see a total of 5.850. 5.850. This is the size of the population in 1991. This is only a sample of this population, comparable with the population of voters in 1997. So this is not necessarily what we really know about the size. This excludes children, who are not eligible to vote in 1997. And for 1997, we have a number as a total, 1.254. This is again an indicative size, not complete population. Voters registered only when they wanted to. There is a group of voters, eligible people, eligible to vote, who did not register or see who was responsible for organising these elections estimates, that the participation was approximately up to 75 per cent also in these areas. So there is a group of voters who are excluded because they didn't register. But still, we believe that this sample size is large enough to obtain relative measures of the ethnic composition that we are discussing right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I may interrupt. We are running out of time, Your Honour. We have a report here. We know that Madam Tabeau is not available until September, so I would kindly ask my learned friend to tell how much in chief we will discuss. Because all these figures, maps, and reports, are in front of the Chamber and in front of the parties. So, Mr. Di Fazio, could you tell us how long you are going to take in chief? Because otherwise we are getting into a serious problem, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not going to be long. I've just about finished, in fact. As I said, I'm only going to go to the major features of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Then please conclude as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you basically comment on the general population movements in the two -- what are now the Serb parts of the former Bosanski Samac and the former Odzak, please. What -- overall, what sort of demographic change have we seen in those two parts of those two former pre-war municipalities?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So it is that I am going to speak now about the population change in these two municipalities. Before the war, in both these municipalities, we observed mixed ethnic composition, practically, even though in one of them there was a majority of Serbs, 55 per cent, in Bosanski Samac. After the war, in both these municipalities, the fraction of Serb population dramatically increased, more than 90 per cent, 92, 93 per cent, and is very much -- and the ethnic composition is very much different from what we used to see there before the war, and not only in this one particular year, 1991, but many, many years before 1991. I must say that these type of changes must be seen as the most dramatic changes of the ethnic composition in the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the size of the changes, the character of the changes, certainly does not allow to see them as regular population change related to population momentum, to how population develops from one year to another. There had to be factors that forced certain groups of people to move out from these municipalities, because I cannot believe that demographic factors or socioeconomic factors could play such a role.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I just ask you to comment on two matters that arise out of the answer. You say that the type of changes seen must be seen as the most dramatic changes of the ethnic composition in the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Are you comparing the changes that took place in Odzak and Bosanski Samac with the rest of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and are you saying that, in those two places, the changes were dramatic, as you say?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I was comparing -- we studied also other municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina, so we can place what we see for these two municipalities in a broader context of changes in other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct of me to say that you do not take the view that these demographic changes can be the result of what one might call, broadly speaking, the usual sort of population changes that one experiences?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said, that the factors, demographic factors, cannot cause these type of rapid changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And finally, would you conclude that the sort of changes that you observed or have studied in those parts of the former municipalities of Odzak and Bosanski Samac are along ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. These were changes along ethnic lines, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have some questions for this witness. Yes. I must inform the Trial Chamber that my learned friend Mr. Lukic and myself, we shall conduct the cross-examination on behalf of all Defence team. We divided our cross-examination. I will take part in questioning of Bosanski Samac on general issues and Mr. Lukic will cover the Odzak area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And some general regions, of course. First of all, I have only, unfortunately, only two coloured maps, map 1 of this region, if the Bench would like to have it to follow. It's just instructive map from the report of Madam Tabeau, but bigger size. It's not evidence. I mean, it's just for the facilitation of following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it the same map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But it's a bigger -- and the settlements are much clearer. If you need. I mean, it's my suggestion. I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can I have this map? Because I don't have this size of map just in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness can have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And we could also have one map for the ELMO and one for Madam Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Tabeau. I am Pantelic, Defence counsel for Mr. Blagoje Simic. Welcome to our proceedings. I didn't interrupt certain line of questioning, including the leading questions from our colleague Mr. Di Fazio, because you two, you are coming from the Prosecution office, so it was kind of internal discussion. Am I right: You are a member of Prosecution office?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, Madam Tabeau, I'm -- well, morning sessions are quite difficult for me; on the other hand, mathematics and statistics are absolutely unknown zone for me, and due to that fact, I went to law school in order to avoid these kind of things, and I would -- I hope that you will help us, all of us here, because basically we are laypersons for these issues. And also, Madam Tabeau, I hope that you would in that sense try to help me because I have a taboo in mathematics and statistics. So maybe you can do your best. First of all, Madam Tabeau --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please put on the ELMO -- this is figure 3 from your report in English, page 30. It's a map of actual Bosnia and Herzegovina. Just a few comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, my understanding is -- well, the map is speaking for itself, of course. The red area is Republika Srpska? Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the green area is Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Consisting of two -- basically, two ethnic groups: Muslims and Croats. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, there are all ethnic groups --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Majority?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- living in the Federation, but these are two major ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Two major ethnic groups. Yes. That was my understanding. Good. And on the basis of Dayton Peace Accord, I mean, these boundaries were settled; is that correct assumption?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please, could you put on the ELMO -- Your Honours, it's on page 27 of the -- Madam Tabeau's report, figure 1A and figure 1B, and I would like to have a few comments on that. Mr. Usher, I would like to have all the page that you have on the ELMO, because there are certain comparative issues. If you can zoom adequately. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My understanding, Madam Tabeau, is that the first map, 1A, is the in fact ethnic composition in -- well, it says by itself, in 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And we all know that Bosnia at that time was like a melting pot with, you know, various ethnic groups in all Bosnia. It was not unique by -- in sense of ethnicity. Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It wasn't homogeneous, yes. There were many ethnic groups living together in many areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Right. Another map is actually the -- well, map speaks for itself. It's also the map based on the Dayton Peace Accord; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is a map which is made without marking the Dayton line, but you certainly can see the Dayton line from the pattern shown in this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. But we would say, to be honest, Madam Tabeau, comparing -- you are free to make a comparison, comparing figure 1B with figure 3, a previous map, we could say that they are more or less the same in terms of boundaries. Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. It is very similar to the reference map that you showed in the beginning of your talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which brings me to the conclusion, Madam Tabeau, that in fact, due to the significant efforts of international community from 1992 -- from Cutilheiro's plan and the other, Vance-Owen plan, and Owen-Stoltenberg plan, et cetera, finally by Dayton Peace Accord plan, in fact, the basis for all these proposals was in fact unification, ethnic unification, more or less. Is that -- would that be a correct assumption?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I object to that question. This witness is not a political expert. She can't comment on the Cutilheiro's plan, the Vance-Owen Plan, and the Dayton Peace agreement as the basis for unification of -- ethnic unification, whatever that might mean. She is not here as a political expert. She is a demographer, and it's unfair on her to ask her questions unless her expertise in the area has been established. It's population and changes in the population that we're concerned with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. I think the Prosecution is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, we shall speak in terms of demographic and statistics issues, of course. We could say that the basis -- first of all, you are familiar with all these peace negotiations; am I correct? You know, in general terms, not details. Madam Tabeau, please. You know Vance-Owen Plan. You are a Ph.D., you are a doctor, you are an educated person. You know Vance-Owen Plan for --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I know many things from different areas, but I really don't feel qualified to say anything about these type of issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. I think we move away from these international agreements and deal with the expert report as it has been presented by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Madam Tabeau. We could agree on the fact that seeing your map, figure 1B, which is on the ELMO now, that there is no areas in Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina where we have Serb majorities. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We have what? I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I am speaking about the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The green and blue area. Could we agree, Madam Tabeau, that according to this map and according to your knowledge, professional and personal, there is no area in Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina where we have a majority of Serbian population? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We don't see it in this map, and this is what I must confirm. Of course, we don't see it on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To be more precise, we don't see --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Majority of Serbs population, of Serb population in the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Again, we don't see the majority, any settlement or any town in the area of Federation where we have majority of Serb population. Am I correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Generally -- well, in order to be a hundred per cent sure, we would have to draw on this map Dayton line and look carefully at all small municipalities located at the Dayton line, and then we will see whether, in these small municipalities, we observe Serb majority or not. But my first general impression, as I see it now, is that we don't see municipalities, we don't show certain ones but just municipalities in this map with Serb majority. I don't exclude that there are small municipalities located at the Dayton line with Serb majority, very small ones. Some of these municipalities at the Dayton line were really extremely small, so you can't see them immediately from the map. You have to study them carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The same approach applies for Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm waiting a little bit between questions because the translation --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- is in the language of our clients. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I don't need, for the moment, this map on the ELMO. We could proceed. And please, put map 1 on the ELMO, the big copy. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong: There is in Geneva, Switzerland, there is headquarters of world demographic organisations, something like that. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In New York, we have a population department of the United Nations, but in Geneva we also have a section analysing population data and producing population statistics, population department, an agency of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is -- actually, there are certain scientific standards in order to fulfil if one country would be in a situation to say, "Well, our census or our procedure is in accordance with the international standards," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understand the question. If we are speaking about standard guidelines --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- for population censuses, I don't think that would be the United Nations and population departments or units of the United Nations who would produce such guidelines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are an expert. Tell me: Is there, in your area of activity, certain guidelines and standards that should be fulfilled by one country to say -- I mean, in international, in terms of international standards, that say, "Well, this census was fair" or, "It was unfair," because there are lots of possibilities for manipulation. It's almost like in elections. So from your point of view, from your professional point of view, is there any -- we know in domestic jurisdictions there are laws, in Poland, in Czechoslovakia -- in Czech Republic, in France, Serbia, Bosnia, we know domestic laws about how the census should go on. I'm asking now: Could you confirm that there are certain standards in international law regarding demographic standards and census that certain countries should fulfil in order to have fair process?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I certainly don't object. I understand what Mr. Pantelic is putting, and I think it's a fair enough question, but it's the way it's phrased. He's asking if in international law there are certain standards and so on. I don't know whether this witness can comment on that. If the question is: Are there internationally accepted guidelines for the conduct of censuses in countries, can you please comment on them? That's fine. I've got no problem with that at all. But it should be phrased along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. My term of international law was strictly related to demographic and statistics issues, not in international law by itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you are asking about internationally accepted standards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Standards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As Mr. Di Fazio put it. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So do we have certain international, recognised standards?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I must say I don't know. I may expect there are such guidelines, but as far as I know, every country is free as to how to apply, induce, these guidelines. This is, first of all, countries' decisions that are involved when conducting censuses. With respect -- another example I certainly know very well from my own work is international classification of diseases, causes of death. There are very, very specific standard guidelines regarding how to code and classify causes of death, and countries actually are almost obliged to follow these rules. But still, there is a certain freedom they have in the way how they apply these guidelines. I expect that the same situation is with censuses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me with the fact that there was an obligation of the national assembly in Bosnia, for example, if you are aware, of course, to confirm the result of census 1991? Are you aware about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, if Your Honours please, it's a question for lawyers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's out of the expertise of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's closely related to the issue. But I will maybe put another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with Polish regulation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not really, because I left Poland ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. At that time, ten years ago --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I didn't work in statistical office on censuses at that time. I worked at the university, so I just don't know whether there is an obligation for the parliament to approve, say, the results of a census. But to be honest, it is rather up to statistical authorities to take the responsibility for the quality and reliability of statistics they produce using censuses and other service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you. Another question which follow after your submission. From your professional background, in fact, I see that you were dealing mostly with mortality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Not with the demographic issue and statistics?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Very much --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Not census, to be honest?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not census as such. I was never involved in conducting census.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go on. I got what I want. Madam Tabeau, tell me: According to your personal and professional knowledge, is there any obligation after the procedure of census to make additional control census, not in the same size, but I would say from one smaller part in order to verify correct results? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: To a certain extent, you are. First of all, before the census is conducted, a pilot survey, like a micro-census, is always completed first, and the results from the pilot are used to improve the question and the way of conducting the proper census. Often, after the census is done, additional surveys, sample surveys, are conducted in order to estimate the errors that are seen in the responses of the participants of that census. Errors are just a part of every survey, including population census, and this is why the additional surveys are often done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And are you aware about the situation in Bosnia in 1991 where they arranged these control census? Are you aware, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't think so. As far as I know, they didn't run any additional surveys after the census. But I might be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Tell me, Madam Tabeau: You spent some time in the archives of Bosnia and Herzegovina, statistic archives, because I'm taking from your report that you developed certain software for checking this, as we say, "maticni broj," the personal number of citizen, and the other forms. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: With the software? Not me myself, but the staff working in our unit and other units indeed developed software to correct mistakes in the names --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- from the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber, please, in short -- well, you said you developed software. Tell me, and tell the Chamber: You were in the mission, in the field in Bosnia. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I was several times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You visited statistic offices and archive of Bosnia and Herzegovina; am I right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I visited Statistical Institute in Sarajevo and also in Banja Luka. I didn't work in the archives of these institutes, not one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But could you explain us when and how you were -- you take certain information about the form of -- for census, where you found all this personal data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We have a copy of the questionnaire in our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of -- here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of all Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You mean the census data, you mean, or the questionnaires? We don't physically have all the questionnaires, because this is a very huge quantity of paper, 4.4 million questionnaires, a questionnaire of several pages, so we don't have possibility to store this type of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting, but I'd like to follow this evidence. I'm having some difficulty here, and I think that Mr. Pantelic ought to clarify with the witness what exactly he's driving at. The witness has mentioned a copy of a questionnaire, and I don't think Mr. Pantelic has established the purpose of the questionnaire, what it was meant to cover, the reason for its existence, and what it was directed at. And unless you know that, it's a bit obscure. And it's not the witness's fault, of course; it's Mr. Pantelic's because he's not clarifying that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, in the report of Madam Tabeau, she speaks about the special software developed in the Office of the Prosecution, where they checked certain important data from census in 1991, and therefore, that is a basis for my questioning: What was the sources for this report, how Madam Tabeau finally found the numbers, ethnicity background, ethnic background, et cetera, which is relevant to her report, the way, the procedure. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I'm grateful to my learned friend. I think I understand now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, you gave us certain digits, figures here. I'm asking you, very directly: Did you make a scanning of the questionnaires? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I understand your question, and we didn't scan the data. We obtained electronic copies of the data, which was scanned by statistical authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And which is now in your possession, because you have to have materials to give your report. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was the basis of my questions. And probably we could put on the ELMO and you could confirm -- I'm not so sure, but this is a form of the 1991 questionnaire in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Am I correct? Madam Tabeau, could you confirm that this is some kind of questionnaire or form that you are familiar and accustomed from the census 1991?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I believe so. I only know the B/C/S language, say -- not definitely, but I can understand it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But this is only one part of the complete questionnaire. There are many more questionnaires.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go to another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have that marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have that document marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's only one copy. Maybe I can do that during the break, enough copies, and then I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But we still have to have it marked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That has to be marked now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or maybe I can tender it now and maybe the registrar would be so kind to make in certain copies for us. Only one copy we need, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I object to its being tendered at the moment. I ask that it be marked for ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, for ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have it marked for identification purposes only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in the mean -- sorry. Sorry. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D48/1 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is its title, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a questionnaire for census.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps a more accurate version would be: Extract from a questionnaire. And given what the witness has said, she said there's a lot more material, and that's just one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what are we going to call it? Extract from questionnaire. Does it have a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, I'm not trying to be difficult but, I mean, the witness hasn't even identified what it is. She doesn't read B/C/S; we haven't had any of it translated. It might be a health insurance form for all I know, if you want to do it strictly speaking. I just don't know. It probably is part of the questionnaire, but there's nothing on the record that shows clearly what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What it is, yes. Let's just have it marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another question, Madam Tabeau: Did you obtain all these data that we have spoken about from Federation, as well as from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: To be honest, I didn't myself obtain the data. I just found the data in my office when I arrived here. So it was someone else who collected these data from Bosnia. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. My understanding is that you don't know whether a part was from Federation of Bosnia and the part was Republika Srpska. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't know, but the data is complete in the sense that it covers the whole country, the whole Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you very much, Madam Tabeau. Allow me now to go in the -- into the merit of our case, in fact. You -- probably you are familiar with the indictment in this case.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I've read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You know that your colleagues from Prosecution office claim that Serbs in Bosanski Samac, in Odzak, allegedly expelled around 17.000 non-Serb population? Am I --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, if it is in the indictment. I don't remember exactly the numbers, but I believe you are referring precisely to the numbers --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good. Okay. My first question, maybe you can have a piece of paper, because we shall have a number of figures and digits here, if it is comfortable with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I would like to have this map on the ELMO again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, according to the, I would say, unofficial, unofficial data of census 1991, could we agree on the fact that in speaking about the municipality of Bosanski Samac, the total population of non-Serbs was 16.964?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I don't object to the question. I understand what Mr. Pantelic is saying. But if the witness goes on to answer the question, there might be some view to some tacit acceptance that there is unofficial data of census. I don't recall the witness saying that there is unofficial data of the census of 1991. If she has said it, I don't recall her saying that. I think that's something that Mr. Pantelic has come up with. So I don't mind the rest of the question, that's fine, but what unofficial data?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify that, my dear friend Mr. Di Fazio, I will just put the answer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, could you confirm that this census from 1991 was never officially proclaimed, and these are just, I would say, quite precise but not official data of the census 1991? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you that the data is unofficial. Why? Because, first of all, there were several publications presenting ethnic composition at municipal level and also settlement level, and I have these publications in my office. I believe one of those publications is in your hands right now. Croatia published one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. We shall --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Let me finish. I must say, I compared statistics from our data with those officially published, and I believe we have the same data. So I don't know what you mean by "unofficial." For me, if statistical authorities in a country issue a publication with official statistics, their official statistics, for me it is official.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. We shall discuss that in Defence case. Don't worry, Madam Tabeau. Let's go to the subject-matter. So could you agree with me that in municipality of Bosanski Samac, according to the census 1991, lived 16.964 non-Serb population, meaning Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In 1991, you mean? I believe more than that, as far as I see it here in table 3, page 7 in the report. The figures presented in this table come from an official publication that is mentioned as a source under the table. And as I see in this table for 1991, we have 13.628 Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- and the total population --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I must interrupt you. Sorry. According to your table - I'm speaking about the 1991 data for Croats - could we agree that it's 14.731? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And could we agree that for the Muslims, the digit is 2.233? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you are -- these are figures already in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, now I want to establish the basis, so I'm just simply asking: Speaking about Croats and Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. My point is, you are asking the witness questions which are already contained in the report, so you objected to that when the Prosecution was doing what you objected to. Can you just ask questions you want to ask the witness without making her repeat what is already contained in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is a mathematical operation, Your Honour, which will follow, and this is a basis; this is a start. This is my basic knowledge about mathematics, you know. And I just want to establish the number of Croats and Muslims in Bosanski Samac municipality, and my question was very simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, given the fact of these two numbers, these two figures, could we agree that non-Serb population, consisting of Croats and Muslims in Bosanski Samac municipality, is 16.964? Because nowhere in your report -- we don't have this data in total. We have only particulars. So could you agree with me? You are better --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You are very correct and your mathematics is fine. The sum of Muslims, number of Muslims and Croats, is 16.964.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Let's start from this figure, finally. Okay. That was 1991.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But this is not the non-Serb population in this municipality --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- because you realise that there are other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the indictment, Madam Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We have a problem here, that your colleague from Prosecution claims that Serbs expelled Croats and Muslims in approximate number of 17.000. So my question is here related to Muslims and Croats, okay?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, but approximately 17.000 and 16.964 is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. But please, let's go to another topic. Are you aware, Madam Tabeau, of the data of how many persons from Bosanski Samac municipality, at the time of 1991 census, were abroad as the workers in Western European countries? Because that was a very often situation in former Yugoslavia. Do you have knowledge about the figures?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not right now, but I can provide you a number later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But I can do that maybe -- because, well, I am the lawyer. I'll try to do my best. I have data with me, and since -- I don't know how we can discuss that, but -- Okay. I will give you my numbers, you can check, and then you will be back. But now let's go with the cross-examination. During the break you can confirm --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. Before you move on to that: You mentioned that the indictment speaks of the expulsion of Croats and Muslims, but you also mention specifically, page 39, line 25 and following, that the indictment speaks of the number of 17.000. Now, to my knowledge, the indictment does not mention a specific number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's paragraph 35 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Tabeau, I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: However, it does speak of non-Serb civilians, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. You forgot your own document, my dear friend. Croats and Bosnian Muslims. End of story. You will check that during the break. And I think it's a break now. It's time for a break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, can you organise your questions so that we don't waste a lot of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then Madam Tabeau can check.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I have a data, Madam Tabeau, that, according to the census of 1991, from Bosanski Samac municipality, abroad were 2.931 persons, and plus, and plus, 1.033 persons as members of family.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Members of their families; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Plus members of their family, yes. Because former Yugoslavia was very much interested about how much money they are earning, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For Odzak, Your Honour, maybe I can give the data, too. For Odzak, it's 4.923, plus members of family, 1.559. So these two data are of our interest. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: As Mr. Pantelic observed, it's time for the break, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: However, just before we break, if Mr. Pantelic is going to show the witness any figures -- or sorry, any documents containing --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. No, no, no. I don't have any intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well. However, after the break, I will be objecting to any further questioning unless there is some sort of identification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Identification to the witness precisely what the source is of this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, wear in the area where maybe our friend is not so familiar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall adjourn the proceedings and continue at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Allow me to address the Chamber with the other issue. It's quite important. Your Honour, we are in situation that we need audiotape of hearing of 8th of July, because next week we shall proceed with the cross-examination of Witness A. It's of crucial importance for us, and we are facing certain problems in that regard, because we filed this request, but probably it will be in seven or more days, and then Witness A will leave the Tribunal. So if Madam Registrar can do something so that we can get that by next Monday, it would be the great importance for the Defence. Thank you. We shall see later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But this is a witness -- you were in court when the witness was giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there is some, I would say, discrepancies of his answers and what was recorded, and then we would like, during the cross-examination, to clarify that issue, but without audiotape we cannot do that. And then if we shall be able to get this in seven or more days, the witness will leave the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But those are matters which you can clarify during cross-examination. You don't necessarily need an audiotape, because you were in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but he already denied, during our intervention, Your Honour, and then we are stuck, we are blocked. Without this proof, material proof, we can do nothing. That's the reason, specific reason, why we are asking the assistance of Trial Chamber with regard to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, prior to the break, we have discussed the matter of the citizens of municipality of Bosanski Samac in 1991 who were abroad. Is that correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And according to my sources and my data here, which are actually part of this official results of census of 1991, I gave you certain numbers.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you check that in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I was only able to find our source for this type of information, but these figures are shown separately for each country, and ethnicity, and someone is now aggregating the figures. So I can submit a copy from the source with partial figures, and the totals will be available later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the basic issue, Madam Tabeau, is that you saw the questionnaire probably during your preparation of your report. You saw the questionnaire and then there is a part in that questionnaire of these citizens who are living and working abroad. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And according to these sources, we have these figures. So I don't know which document you have, but simply, we are speaking about the certain number of persons of Bosanski Samac municipality who were, at the moment of census 1991, abroad?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm just not following this at all. Is Mr. Pantelic referring to that extract of the questionnaire that was given an exhibit number -- I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It was numbered for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, numbered for identification, first of all. Is that what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that what Mr. Pantelic -- okay. Perhaps we should put that into the record of the evidence so that we're clear, and that's D-ID, whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's D48/1 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the Chamber for that. And then

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC SAYS
utterances.text: "And according to these sources, we have these figures." I don't know what sources and what figures he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. If you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the results of census of 1991 for Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because you can confirm, of course, Madam Tabeau --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Where is the document you are dealing with?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's just information -- it's an extract from the report. It's a fact of common knowledge, as I can say, because this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, my aim, Your Honour, during cross-examination, is to show that this witness didn't include that important figure. So there is no -- this figure is not in this report, and that's a line of my cross-examination because it brings us to certain situation where we can manipulate with the figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. But the point is, if you are challenging the witness with figures from another source, you must identify that source. Because how does it help the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will clarify that with the witness because we are speaking about the same issue, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How does the Trial Chamber know whether that source of yours is official?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, this is the -- how I can say? Like --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, you are familiar with the cross-stat, Croatian book that you made certain references in your report? Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This one, I see front page of this publication. I don't know what is inside that you have there, but this is the front page of the publication.
