utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And you can agree with me, and to help this Chamber, with the fact that all data during one census, including the ethnic background, identification number, number of children, property, et cetera, also the presence abroad, is practically the basis for results of census? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The questions from the questionnaire are indeed used to produce certain statistics, and then we see this type of publications, as the one you showed us, the front page you showed us, with just aggregate statistics with figures related to municipalities or settlements and showing ethnic composition, other variables like income, socioeconomic situation of individuals covered by the census, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And during your work, during your professional activity, it came to your attention data with regard to the number of citizens working abroad. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It was a very commonly known fact that citizens of the former Yugoslavia were allowed to freely move abroad and to work there, and of course this was also the case with people from these two municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And my question was: Did you personally come to that fact while examining the sources from statistical -- Bosnia-Herzegovina statistical institute or whatever?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: To publications, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. I'm speaking about these particular figures of the citizens working abroad. Did you -- did it come to your attention?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I brought here a copy from a publication issued by the statistical -- by the Institute for Statistics. It is, I believe, the federal institute who published that, although -- no. The year of publication is 1994. It is just publication of the Statistical Office of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I have these figures, official statistics. I am not sure whether these figures and your figures are the same, but these figures I have are definitely non-zero figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. So, well, my idea was just if you can confirm my figures, because I have these figures also from the same source, I would say statistical basis for this particular issue. So if you cannot agree, you say so. No problem.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I have some --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We are speaking -- excuse me. We are speaking about, as I said, 2.931 from Bosanski Samac --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please. If Your Honours please, I'll explain my objection. Mr. Pantelic, I hope, will listen and reply. My objection is very simple. If Mr. Pantelic wants to put figures of people who are working overseas from the Bosanski Samac and Odzak municipalities, or indeed for the country as a whole, I have no objection at all, no problem with that at all. But he has to identify his source so the expert can comment upon the source and then upon the figures. That's the proper way of doing it. He cannot just simply mention in court, without giving anything to the witness, figures, because you don't know the origin of the figures, I don't know the origin of the figures, the witness doesn't know the origin of the figures. And so I've got no problem with his endeavouring to do what he was trying to do. On the contrary; I encourage it. But do it with some proper documentation or some proper source of the figures and then the witness can say, "Yes," "no," "I agree," or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Otherwise, the information is a waste of time. You've been asked about the source. I think this is the fourth time. You appear to be reluctant to produce it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour. Please understand me. I'm speaking about the source which is in the possession of Prosecution office, Your Honour. They are in possession. They scanned everything from Sarajevo. They scanned questionnaires. They --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: They are in possession of these sources, not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is that document you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have just an extract of the official census of 1991 with regard to the ethnicity, with regard to the compilation from 1971, 1961, 1953, and all other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Where did you get that extract?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In a bulletin in manual of this census of 1991, which is in possession exactly of the Prosecution. And Madam Tabeau confirmed that. So I don't know how I can operate with their sources and their data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: They are in possession, Your Honour, not me. It's a fact of common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where is the mountain, what is the exact figure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we clear this, then? Mr. Di Fazio, is it the document that the witness has? Can we clear this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've not seen either of the two documents. I've not seen the document that the witness got wherever from during the break, and I've not seen the document that Mr. Pantelic has. I don't know. That's why I'm saying that the -- that he should put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, maybe we can resolve this. Can you get the document the witness has been referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, can you be quiet?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are just two pages taken out from a larger document and copied together with the front page of this publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would like to ask a question, put a question to Mr. Pantelic. By your examination now, are you trying to question the credibility of the witness or the credibility of her report? Give me a straight answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Gladly. Gladly, Your Honour. This witness is a part of Prosecution team. The position of the Defence is that this witness is biased, one-sided, and the report is not -- report is to some extent a manipulation of figures, which means, Your Honour -- I will give you an example. We have a number of 1.000. We could say whether in this number of 1.000, 300 are here or there, or we cannot speak about that. The census, Your Honour, is a large area of various sources, and I, hypothetically, as an expert, I would say, "Well, from this area, I pick this flower but I don't take this flower." And then in my cross-examination I'm challenging the way, the methods, and approach of this witness. And it is not my duty to have in my possession all these data. This witness is a well-established and experienced expert and she should know about what we are talking, and she should be ready, with all these data in front of her, not only this report. Because you are a very well-experienced person, Your Honour. You know how the figures can be manipulated. And I will show -- I will explain just right now what is the manipulation in this report. That is the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've got no problem with Mr. Pantelic attacking the credibility of the witness, and by doing so with statistics, with numbers, figures. If he wants to show that the figures that the witness has produced have failed to take into account numbers of people from Bosanski Samac and Odzak working in Europe at the time, fine. I've got no problem with that. I encourage him to do that. But if he's going to put figures to the witness, show her the document and the source so that she can comment upon it. That's simply, in a nutshell, what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I reply just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic. The witness has got a document, and can we have it -- because we haven't got it marked, we haven't got it described.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, can we have the title of the document you are discussing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a publication based on the -- this is not the title what I'm saying. I don't want to translate because I am not an interpreter. I want to explain briefly what is this. This is not the publication of the basic census data as the one Mr. -- I'm sorry, I've forgotten your name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pantelic showed us a moment ago. This was a different publication that contains information about ethnic composition and only ethnic composition of the population in municipalities and settlements in the whole country, in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The publication I brought with me is something else. In addition to this type of publication as the one Mr. Pantelic showed us, every statistical office produces additional publications, sorts of bulletins that only contain selected information from the census. The information I brought with me is related only to population working abroad and families of this population staying with them abroad. And this is, in this publication, done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is for the census -- it shows census data. It was published in the year 1994, but the data shown here is from 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I extracted two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Double-printed from this publication. One page is Bosanski Samac, one page is Odzak. It is very likely that my information is hundred per cent consistent with the figures you gave me, but I don't know this yet because these figures here are given by country of residence of those working abroad, and you gave me total numbers of all persons working abroad, without distinguishing among the countries. So I have to aggregate the figures, and this is already being done by someone in my office, and later today we can see that ourselves. But I think the intention is here to speak about those who resided abroad at the moment of the census and were physically absent in the two municipalities in that time. And I agree there were such people who worked abroad, who resided in other countries, even though they were included in the census. This is my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And one should expect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. One further question. You are now talking about the figure of, if I understand you right, correctly, about 2.500 from the municipalities of Bosanski Samac and Odzak, abroad, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. The total for Samac, with members of family, is 4.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. 4.000. 2.500 and 4.000. It doesn't matter. But if you look at Article 28 in the indictment, the Prosecution is talking about a total number of 17.000. So I'm just interested in what's the relevance of your line of questioning about 2.500 or 4.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. This is just the beginning of the mathematical operation that I will bring to your attention. The bottom line is that we shall show that the Prosecution completely erred, and furthermore, they tried to -- well, I will not explain that. Anyhow, we have -- I will show you in a couple of minutes what was the situation with the population in Bosanski Samac. It is just beginning, Your Honour. It is just beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now, I wanted to ask Mr. Di Fazio about the document which the witness has been -- has brought out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Would you like it marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I would. I would like it marked for identification. She's referred to it in her evidence, and clearly it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number, please? Although we just have one copy which is with the witness, it will be surrendered later, I think. It will be marked for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be P134 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, since -- well, you are not at the moment familiar, but you will check, of course, although you confirm that there was such a number. Okay. I gave you two figures. You remember? 2.931 plus members of the family, 1.033, from Bosanski Samac municipality, working abroad.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we agree on the fact -- it is a well-known fact, in fact, you said that the percentage of Croats in Bosanski Samac municipality in 1991 was 45 per cent. Am I correct? This is --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: - page 1 of your --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. In the whole municipality, pre-war municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Serbs 41 per cent. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Muslims, 7 per cent. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Or a little bit more. Approximately, say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's say --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Although the Defence claims that -- probably you should not -- you are not in a situation to know that, but let me explain that in this way: Around 80 per cent of workers abroad were Croats. We know that from the area, you know, from checking ID. But now we cannot introduce that percentage. And I suggest - and correct me if I'm wrong - to use official and your percentages of the ethnic structure, for example, Croats, 45 per cent, plus 7 per cent of Muslims, which is 52 per cent. Could we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, these are figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Why I'm asking you to help me and to help the Chamber with these percentages? Because the number of workers abroad, which are around 4.000, we could now examine with 52 per cent, and we could say, after - it was quite complicated operation for me, I must admit - but 55 per cent of this number brings me to 2.061.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But I don't understand. Why do you apply this per cent to the number, total number of those working abroad? There is no reason to apply such an assumption that the ethnic composition of those working abroad and the ethnic composition in the municipality were the same. I don't think they were the same. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In order to help this Trial Chamber, in order to help to find the truth. Madam Tabeau --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you've understood the question that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I will give the explanation. Yes. Absolutely. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, we are speaking about the population -- you remember that we are speaking about the population of Croats and Muslims, which is 16.964, according to the census. Now we have around 4.000 citizens, people, no matter which ethnicity, abroad. What I'm trying to establish, because you are familiar with the issues, with the voters register in 1997, which is completely different than the census of 1991, so we have to establish certain standards. Help me if I'm correct. I would like to say that applying the proportion of 52 per cent of the population in Bosanski Samac consisting of Muslims and Croats, in total number of 4.000, says that 2.061, more or less, Muslim and Croats were abroad. You know, we have to establish certain matters.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But there is no need to do so because the data I already submitted is given by ethnicity of those working abroad. So why should we estimate it? It's a matter of just adding up the numbers by ethnicity, and we know it exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree. So we could simply -- because, you know, we are speaking about Serbs, Muslims, and Croats, Madam Tabeau, and I would not say from this initial figure of 16.000, where we are speaking about Muslims and Croats, I don't want to deduct number of 4.000, where we are including Serbs, then we should have our own conclusion. So that was my own suggestion to help me, whether we could consider this ethnic structure, saying of 4.000 people abroad, 52 per cent were Muslim and Croats, which brings us to amount of 2.000. That was my idea.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Intention. But I think it is important to know, right now, that the census actually reports the population who actually lived in this area, stayed physically, at the moment of census. So it is -- those who were abroad were just abroad, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Respect -- I must --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So there is no need to speak about the population staying abroad in the context of the figures I presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. Yes, yes, yes, but I think you are wrong and we shall -- I will explain you why you are wrong. Respectfully, I think that you are wrong. You have a total of population, according to the census of Bosanski Samac, of 32.960, and then divided by the ethnic groups. In these groups actually are included peoples abroad. That's -- you know, that's a general figure, and then there are various figures in that figure. So probably you should check your data, because --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If you could give me a source that shows that it is indeed that workers abroad and their families are in the totals presented, because I am not sure that you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I get it from the official statistics that you have in possession. So maybe it's a matter of dispute. We shall resolve that. I mean, you can change --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I didn't see this type of figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed with your proposition. Could you agree with me that we could deduct this number of 4.000 from 16.000?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, I cannot, because in my view, they are not included in this 16.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: They are not included?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's your position. Good.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I must check this to be hundred per cent sure, but as far as I understand my figures, it is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do that when you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Where you just mentioned on line 13, page 57, that you've got your information from the official statistics that Ms. Tabeau has in her possession, I'd like to know where, you know, what page or something further, something more concrete, if there is this dispute as to where the information is that you're relying on versus the information that Ms. Tabeau is relying on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, Your Honour. I will gladly explain that. Madam Tabeau and the Prosecution are in possession of the official questionnaires. They scanned it in Sarajevo. She confirmed that. They are in possession of all official documents, including official bulletins, official editions like this one, like this one from Zagreb, and she made certain reference to that. These are statistical books, Your Honour, and she knows very well. And I'm now saying and outlining that we know - this is a matter of science, Your Honour - that these people working abroad are actually included in the number of total population of Bosanski Samac municipality, and very easily we shall prove that with our expert during the Defence case. The problem here is that this witness, with all due respect, is not ready for the cross. She is not in possession of all these necessary data. Because probably the Defence will not open the cards prior to the cross. So we can expect that this witness will be armed with all these sources. So we are speaking about official sources from Sarajevo of the statistics. But let's move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's not move on, if Your Honours please. Your Honour asked a perfectly reasonable question, and before Your Honour did, I was about to ask very much the same question. Figures are being put to the witness for which there is absolutely not one skerrick of evidence, not one -- nothing, nothing at all. They are just figures that are coming out of the blue. The witness has repeatedly said that the figures that she used in her report do not take into account people who were living away, living in Europe. So they're absolute figures. That's the end of the matter. Now, if Mr. Pantelic wants to show that the figures do include people who were in fact working in Switzerland or in fact working in Turkey or wherever, let him put it to the witness so she can say, "Yes, I'm wrong. I can see your point." But that's not being done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my consultant, my demographic consultant, just gave me these figures, and he said that in scientific world, it is a fact of common knowledge that these figures came from the official bulletins. And I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. I think let's sort it out this way. If the Defence are saying that the figures they are putting forward, they will be able to show in the Defence case, then let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. That was my position. And we shall with our evidence show how this witness is unreliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, Madam Tabeau, speaking about the other number, we have on the ELMO map of pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac, and speaking about Bosanski Samac, and map speaks for itself. The black line is a border of pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac, in the legend it says. That's correct; yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, but I said in the beginning that this map is just an illustration and that we don't -- we shouldn't take it very literally that every line marked on this map is exactly the same as in reality

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Madam Tabeau, it's illustration. Call it how you want it. No problem, it's illustration. It's not reliable source. But still, it's a part of your report. Anyhow, so could we agree that in your, this such -- call it illustration or sketch, whatever, the black line is the border of the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac? Am I correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Which black line?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Show --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Take the pointer and show -- okay. Take the pointer and show the Chamber what is the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The witness did that twice in examination-in-chief, from what I recall, possibly three times. What's the point of the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, we could agree, Madam Tabeau, that in 1995 Dayton Peace Accord was introduced, and you explained it very well that the red lines are showing the number of the territory of pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac now in Federation. Now, Madam Tabeau, could you agree with me that 8.200 non-Serb citizens, namely, Muslims and Croats, are in the territory out of Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, according to the Dayton line? Could you confirm, or you cannot confirm, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: How can I see that from this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, not from this map. Madam Tabeau, you should see from your source which is called cross-stat, and you make certain references in your report, and I will refresh your memory. First of all, are you familiar with the fact that Domaljevac -- could you show to the Chamber where is Domaljevac on the map? Just take a pointer and show -- mark -- put your pointer on the document.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Could you agree with me that from the source that you make certain references in Domaljevac according to census of 1991, there were 4.072 Croats? Could you confirm or not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: How many you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I said 4.072 Croats.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I see 4.597.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It's my mistake. Sorry, because I didn't --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Table 4, page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Okay. Yes, yes. That's my mistake. I made it. Plus Muslim population here, so that -- you are right. So we could agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting, Mr. Pantelic, but just for the sake of clarification, I want to make sure that I understand your question on page 60, beginning line 22, correctly. If you go to the third line of that question, which is line 24, you talk about -- sorry. Sorry, page 61, line 1. You talk about Muslims and Croats are in the territory out of Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac. And I'm not certain what you're meaning by "are in the territory out of Serbian municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. Yes, I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, you showed the parts north of red line where Domaljevac is, and then west of the red line where Prud is. These are the territories now in the territory of Federation of -- Muslim Croat Federation. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also, in fact, these territories are a part of pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We are speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is that, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prud?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Does that satisfy your inquiry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. I understand the questions and the answers now. I think it was just the phraseology in that line I pointed out which was unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My English is far from good, so I am really facing certain linguistic troubles. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. You have number of 4.597 in Domaljevac Croat population, plus certain number of -- or includes Muslims in that number. Yes. Is that correct, Madam Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I mentioned 4.597 Croats --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- living in Domaljevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: According to census, it was 7 Muslims in Domaljevac. Probably you know -- probably, you don't know anyhow. But it's not so significant number, so let's stick to your figure. Let's stick to your number. Okay. That's not in dispute. Are you familiar, Madam Tabeau, that in village of Basik, which is also in the territory north of this bordering line of Samac, was, according to census of 1991, 526 Croats? Are you familiar or you are not familiar?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I must say, I don't know all the numbers for all settlements from my head. I could check this, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Are you familiar with the fact that according to the census of 1991, official data, of course -- I'm always relying to your sources when I'm speaking about these data, Your Honours. I'm relying to the cross-stat which was mentioned in her report. So I just simply take this edition and I'm speaking with this witness. So, Madam Tabeau, could you confirm that in Grebnice -- could you show Grebnice, please? This is on the upper side of --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you confirm that in Grebnice, which is now in Muslim Federation, there is 1.933 Croats? Can you confirm or you cannot?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I don't remember all numbers because these are thousands of numbers published in this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. But we are speaking now about criminal proceeding case and I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. The questions must be fair to the witness. She can't remember. You can just be putting them to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And she can't be expected to remember all those tiny, tiny details.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then, Madam Tabeau, are you familiar with the number in Prud, according to the census 1991, a number of 1.144 Croats?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: As I said before, the same story. I can check this and confirm later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. The total number of Croats in these actually settlements of the Bosanski Samac municipality in 1991, you have confirmed that Domaljevac, Basik, Grebnice, and Prud are now in the territory of Muslim-Croat Federation. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is how we see it from this map, but in order to be hundred per cent sure, I would refer to the OSCE classification scheme, which shows precisely how to classify settlement, to which municipality they belong. Prud, I know for sure is not part of Domaljevac Samac. It is now part of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking about pre-war municipality. Okay. My calculation shows that 8.200 Croats lived practically in the pre-war municipality of Samac, in the territories which are now a territory of Muslim-Croat Federation. Am I correct with my position?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You might be correct, but we said already in the beginning -- I said that Domaljevac is a Croatian municipality, 90 per cent -- 98 per cent of Croats there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: You are mixing up the municipalities, because Prud was a part of Odzak and not a part of Bosanski Samac. So you can't include the people living in Prud into the people living in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, it is not the case. In fact, Prud was a part of pre-war Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. You see the line left of the Prud -- black line, and our --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pre-war, yes. Pre-war, but not post-war. The thing is that the borders changed, sometimes very considerably, after Dayton, and Prud, actually, is a very good example of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is moved to the other municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This calculation, Madam Tabeau, brings me to conclusion that calculation of 8.200 Croats living in Grebnice, Basik, Prud, and Domaljevac, and everything -- Madam Tabeau can check that during the break, her source that she relied upon.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: What was the last settlement? Domaljevac, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Domaljevac. I said Grebnice, Basik, Domaljevac, and Prud. We can check that during the break. Okay. What I would like to say: These Croats were not displaced. They stayed in the same territory where they lived in 1991. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is what I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- in the beginning of my testimony; at least, I said it very explicitly for the municipality Domaljevac/Samac, excluding Prud.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. For the purposes of our cross-examination, we have to include Prud because Prud was a part of pre-war municipality Bosanski Samac, and that is why it's important, why it's important for our case. That brings me to number of -- when I -- when I deduct 8.200 from the number of, let's say -- well, it's in dispute, but my way is that the workers abroad are included in these figures, et cetera, et cetera. So that brings me to the conclusion that the Croat population still lived in Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now we have a figure of 6.703, because we have to be focused on the issue of our case. There is an assumption, there is an allegation from the Prosecution, that 17.000 Croats and Muslims were expelled. Now I'm showing that a significant number still stayed on the same place where they were in 1991. But are you familiar with the fact, Madam Tabeau, that in village of Kornica -- can you find on the map village of Kornica? Ill help you. Kornica is actually on the -- you see Modrica, on the south. Below letter "A" of Modrica, you will find Kornica. Did you find that settlement?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I must say, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You know where is Modrica?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Find letter -- no, no. The letters of "Modrica."

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to help you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Perhaps you can take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Below -- I cannot approach. Below the letter "A" of "Modrica," go below, and you will see on the border this name "Kornica"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Modrica, the one in bigger letters, on the white part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Big letter. Yes, yes, that's correct. Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another -- just go to the right, to your right, from Kornica, and you will see Srednja Slatina.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. During your preparation of your report, are you familiar, Madam Tabeau, that prior to the end of June 1992, before the military operation called Corridor, the complete population of these two villages - in total, I'm speaking about Croats, in total is 1.720 - left this area to the territory where the Croats were controlling that area? Are you familiar or are you not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I am not. Well, we are speaking about 1991, population census, and you are now mentioning 1992, prior to June 1992, so I assume you are speaking about first months of the year 1992. And you are referring to population movements, outflow of Croats, this number you mentioned from these two settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Since you are a member of Prosecution office, so I thought maybe you were in discussion, proofing. Just say no. No problem.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, no. I am working independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I take your answer as "no."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you should allow the witness to complete the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So I wanted to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- stress that I am an independent demographer, even though I'm part of the Prosecutor office. And I do my work to the best of my knowledge and my skills, and I use sources that I believe are reliable and can be presented here in Court. This is what I do. And I don't communicate every single detail with the trial team.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's understandable, perfectly understandable. No problem, Madam Tabeau. This calculation brings me to another subtotal, which is -- I'm speaking about the population of Croats and Muslims with regard to the first number, and now it brings me to a subtotal of 4.983. Now we are going to your page 8 of your report, when you are speaking about split settlements. You will see that, in fact, the number of Croats were 3.004 and Muslims was 7. In total, it's 3.011, and the position of the Defence is that this population actually was now physically in the territory of Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't follow you. I didn't follow you, the numbers. I couldn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Page 8 of your report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in front of my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You see first item, which is split settlement?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You see the Croats: 3.004? [Realtime transcript read in error: "3.000 004"]

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You see Muslims: 7?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Total is 3.011.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, the position of the Defence is the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, correction in line 11. 3 million, well, court recorder, give us -- it's a correction. It's not, of course -- page 69, line 11, it is not 3 million and 4 Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the figure?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Figure is 3.004

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We said earlier that we have 3.004 Croats, plus 7 Muslims, according to your report, and it brings us to 3.011. Madam Tabeau, the position of Defence is the following: Although you didn't include this number of 3.011 in your calculation, the Defence is of the opinion and position that this number of 3.011 should be included in the territory of Federation of Muslim-Croat Federation, and we have to deduct our subtotal of 4.983 with these 3.011. And I will put you certain questions with that regard. Could you agree with me that the settlement Doljani --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I don't mind the general line of the cross-examination, but surely the witness should be -- what's happening here is that Mr. Pantelic is making a statement: This is the truth of the matter or this is the situation or this is what we say, and then goes on to ask a different question. When you come to read the transcript, it's going to be very difficult to understand exactly what the witness is saying and what she is meaning. Why can't Mr. Pantelic ask the witness to comment upon that calculation? After all, that's the purpose that she is here, it's the reason why she is here, the calculation and the methods of including -- and the reasons why various numbers are included.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm laying -- sorry, my learned friend. I'm laying my foundation, Your Honour. We have to clarify the foundation and then I'm going with the examination. Our position, my learned friend, is that your expert did not include 3.011 Croats and Muslims in the territory of Muslim-Croat Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's our position. That's our foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Terrific. Wonderful.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now I'm proceeding with certain line of questioning, to see whether your expert is familiar with the issues that we are discussing. If your expert is not familiar, then the Trial Chamber will draw certain conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No objection to the question. No objection. But can the witness comment on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- the proposition. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Allow the witness to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Now I will pose a question and then she can comment. Of course. Gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, let me clarify things. There is certain settlements, because I have a bigger map, and I make certain changes. This, by the way, is Prosecution map of UNPROFOR operational map series which was submitted well in advance. I don't know. It was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Was it produced in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. It's just for my -- because I have to follow the names of the settlements. It's just for my - I don't know - notes or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But now, tell me, Madam Tabeau: Are you aware of the settlement or village Doljani, which is north of line -- of bordering line of Dayton? It is not on your map, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Isn't it this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is also called Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Doljani, you have?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: And it is likely that it is a split settlement or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Okay. Yes, yes, yes. Sorry. My mistake. Okay. So Doljani is in this line of split settlements. Are you aware also of the settlement of Vranica, although it is not on your map, but it's also in the same area?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is on my map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Vranica.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Just on the Dayton line, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, just on the Dayton line. Yes, that's correct. Are you aware about the Tursinovac?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is also on my map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware about the Odmut?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't see it on my map, I must say, but if you see it, if you could show me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a problem with the ... Correct me if I'm wrong: North of Doljani, is there a Masici settlement? Because it's not so good copy.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Probably. But indeed, the font is very unclear and we cannot read.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then also we have in your map a settlement Snoge? Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. So all this area, split settlements, according to your report, consist of 3.011 Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I mentioned in table 4, on page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Why you -- or could you agree with me, of course, that in fact all Croats and Muslims, in total of 3.011, are now living on the territory of Muslim-Croat Federation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, this is something that I cannot agree with, because I said that split settlements were actually excluded from the analysis because they were split. This means that part -- one part of each split settlement was in the Federation, another one in Republika Srpska. And these are split settlements not because I split them but because they were split due to -- according to the Dayton Peace Agreement. And OSCE, organisation responsible for establishing a classification scheme for statistical analysis, like my work, didn't include them as part of the federal or Serbian municipality. They are just split, so you need specific addresses of every citizen in order to include these persons either to the Federation or to Republika Srpska. I didn't have this information to use in my work. This is why split settlements were excluded entirely from any municipality. They were just left aside from the analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But, Madam Tabeau, we could agree that in these settlements, there are 3.011 Muslims and Croats, could we not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And they are living in their homes in these split settlements, obviously, because you made certain registration, analysis, and then you locate them in these areas. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No. They lived in their houses, likely, but I don't know whether certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. That is my point.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is my point. That is my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness complete her explanation.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That we don't know whether their homes now are Federation or Republika Srpska; at least, I don't know, because I don't have a classification scheme, a guideline, that I could use for me, as a statistician, to include them. I cannot just aggregate individuals using my feeling or intuition. I really always try to use official classification schemes and official documents, guidelines, the so-called guidelines, in doing my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You see, Madam Tabeau, the point is here, from the point of view of Defence, that these people are still in their homes. They were not expelled. They are living in these neighbouring areas. Because you just said that, according to the analysis of voters register, you assigned them, ascribed them, to the split settlements. And my point is not to have academic discussion about where and what it is, but it's very simple. My question is: According to your knowledge, according to your data, could you confirm that these 3.011 Muslim and Croats lives in that split settlements? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I'll answer this question in a different way. I have shown in my report, even excluding the split settlements, that in Domaljevac-Samac, Croats, 98 per cent of the whole population living in this municipality still lived there in 1997, in their own homes. So I said already in my report that those who lived there still lived there after the conflict. But I think what I also tried to do in my report, I tried to look at the other municipalities in this region, and for me, as a demographer, this what happened in the municipalities belonging to Republika Srpska is dramatic because there the ethnic composition changed in a way that I don't see Muslims, Croats, the same way as they used to be there before the war. This is what I am saying. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And also, you confirm that also there is no Serbs in Muslim-Croat Federation. That's the same story. Yes? You said that earlier.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, if you are thinking of a part of Odzak municipality --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. You are speaking about general Bosnia and I'm speaking about general Bosnia. The follow-up question is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The witness is not speaking about general Bosnia. She is talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Just read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If I may be permitted to finish my objection, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The witness isn't talking about general Bosnia. She's talking about the municipalities of Odzak and Bosanski Samac that -- and those parts thereof that belong to the Republika Srpska. That's what she is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Madam Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Not Bosnia in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Municipalities to Republika Srpska is line 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I don't want to argue with you, Madam Tabeau. You showed us, and you can confirm also, that there is no Serb population in Odzak. Yes? Now --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In the federal part?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the federal part.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I showed in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also you can confirm that there is no Serbs in Odzak, is that correct, now in federal part?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Did I show this in my report for Orasje, particularly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, allow the witness to complete the answer. The record will be so confused. Because you keep speaking before she finishes the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. It's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So I agree I showed no Serbs or hardly any Serbs after the conflict in 1997 in the federal part of Odzak. This is what I showed. And I presented -- discussed these figures today, in the morning. But I didn't say anything about Orasje as such in my report, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Speaking about Domaljevac in this part of pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac. But my friend will cover the issue of Odzak. My question was very simple, Madam Tabeau. Let's go back. My question was: Could you agree with me that 3.011 Muslims and Croats, according to your analysis, according to register of voters of OSCE and your sources and your report, are still living in the split settlements, Yes or no? And then we shall move on. Don't give me a broad answer. Just "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I cannot, because the 3.011 Muslims and Croats you mentioned were reported in the 1991 population census, and now you are saying that the same number of Croats and Muslims were registered as voters in 1997, which is not necessarily the truth. The table actually, here, shows 1991 population only. So this is the status before the conflict and not after the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So am I understanding well --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I would have to run a query to check for these persons identified in that census, whether they indeed lived or registered to vote in 1997 in the same settlements or the same at least municipality, and then I can answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. And finally, could we agree, Madam Tabeau, that -- now we are jumping into the other area which is the number of voters. Let's see your table 6B.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Page 13?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, page 13. Speaking about Muslims, in the first column, am I understanding correctly that 187 Muslims voted from the municipality of Samac, Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, it is not correct. They registered to vote in this municipality. There were two location items in the voters register. One was municipality of registration, where people physically registered to vote, and there was another location item, the municipality they wanted to vote for, which is a different story. You physically didn't need to be in a particular municipality to vote for this municipality. And as we all know --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. But, you know, I'm just trying to clarify this table, table 6B. If I understood correctly, 187 Muslims were in municipality of Bosanski Samac, Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Registered to vote, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Registered to vote. Then other municipalities, 349, and then out of country, 505, and then 1.041. Okay. My understanding was -- I'm not speaking where they are and whether they vote or not, because you introduced that matter, and I would like to seek clarification from you. You said that this is number registered in Samac, according to your sources from OSCE documentation. You said this municipality. This municipality means Bosanski Samac RS. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: They were registered in this municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is at least -- we found them as registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Also on the basis -- on the same principle, you registered 104 Croats?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which means that they are voters over the age 18. Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: 18 or more. People eligible to vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good. Would you agree with me that certain number of people don't want to go to vote, and they --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Accordingly, they don't want to be registered. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, because this is election, so you don't have to go. You choose to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So these figures, these digits, are, to some extent, not reliable, for the two reasons: They don't show the population below the age of 18, and then they don't show the real population because we have certain voters which don't want to be registered. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but all that is contained in the report already.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. If I may say, it is not about the reliability of the figures; it is about completeness of the source. And I said in the beginning, when commenting on the sources, that while census is a complete population survey and covers the whole population living in an area, voters register is a sample, a sample that, as estimated by OSCE, covered, in this particular election, approximately 70, 75 per cent of the population. Of course, only certain age groups, not the whole population.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. My question is the following: Madam Tabeau, applying your method, and given the fact of these two issues that I spoke, could we agree that this number of Muslims and Croats registered in municipality of Bosanski Samac RS should be -- on this number should added at least the same number, given the fact that they are not all registered, and then we should say at least 20 per cent of the population less than 18 year? Because my friend, my learned friend, will show you -- afterwards he made certain analysis of how you made these calculations, and then that, according to this calculation, we have approximately 700 Croats and Muslims in the municipality of Samac RS, roughly.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right. You said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not me, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then, according to my calculation, Madam Tabeau, following these standards, I came to the figure of 1.200 Muslim and Croat population, which are approximate number that they left, for different reasons, Bosanski Samac municipality. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't know, but I would like to comment on what you said about the completeness of the figures in table 6B. You said that it is necessary to increase the number by at least the same. I wouldn't agree with that. You could increase the numbers by a certain per cent, according to the participation rate in the election --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I give you my example and then you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let the witness finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I will stop you from cross-examination, because you don't want the witness to complete the answer. You don't want the witness to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll give her my idea and then she can correct me. That may be easiest for all of us. And then she will say no, it is not correct. She's an expert. That was my idea, nothing more. Okay. I agree.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But increasing the number equally by the same percentage is not necessarily a good idea, because those who don't participate in elections are usually very particular groups, and they don't go for certain reasons. So we don't know the ethnic composition of those who didn't register to vote. Well, we always say that we present minimum numbers in our report. It is not that we present complete population size; we speak about minimum population size. And these are the figures in this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but correct me if I'm wrong, Madam Tabeau. We see here 187 plus 104 voters more than 18 years old. Could you agree with me that we have to -- these are voters, but there is a certain number of non-registered voters. Could we increase this number -- what is your suggestion for which percentage we should increase these two digits? Please, tell me.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you wait, Mr. Pantelic? The interpreters are having a problem because you are using the same language. So we have forgotten about pausing to allow the questions to be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Madam Tabeau, we cannot say how many -- what is the percentage of increasing of these people given the fact that there is some passive voters, in fact. You cannot give us the precise answer?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you say 10 per cent, 20, 30?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I wouldn't mention any figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I would have to study the responses of non-registered voters somehow, based on a sample, to say anything more about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I agree with your position, although the figures are a different one. Now I would like to just put to you several questions. I've finished with this kind of analysis. Just several questions about your, I would say, reliability. First of all, Madam Tabeau, I think that, looking at first page of your report, where you bolded, in this subparagraph 4, you bolded the words "Croats and Muslims largely disappeared from Samac." Could we agree with me that the word "disappeared" is not more appropriate? Could we agree upon the maybe better -- maybe "population movement" or "immigration"? Because I clearly -- and I, frankly, don't understand. What does it mean, that they physically disappeared or simply in terms of immigration? Could you be so kind to explain this to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If you feel more comfortable with the expression "moved out" or, I don't know, "migrated out of the municipality." But the meaning is basically the same; they are not physically there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you can understand my worry. The word "disappeared" is a little bit, you know --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If you think of negative connotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We agreed upon the immigration of population movement, stuff like that. Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Looking at page 2 of your report, you also used that word, but we clarified that. But my attention was brought to the word in your last paragraph, "summing up," two clear examples of ethnic cleansing. Tell me, Madam Tabeau, what is the basis and what is your professional knowledge, since you are not a legal expert, to say that it was an ethnic cleansing? You are a scientist, you are a demographer, so could you agree with me that you are not a professional lawyer who knows the notion of ethnic cleansing? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, if there is a legal definition of ethnic cleansing, then I must say, I don't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to another topic.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But let me finish. In --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a cross-examination. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, let the witness explain and complete her answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But as a demographer, when I see that in such a short period of time one ethnic group is completely gone from an area, and this is completely really, indeed, because if it is half a per cent of one per cent who remained out of, say, 40 per cent or something. So for me, as a demographer, it is an ethnic cleansing in the sense of demography. This group is not there any more. So what I meant was demographically speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Not legally. Yes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, not. I am not a legal person. I don't have legal background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I'm a bit annoyed by your questioning of the witness. I'm coming from a system where I have been used to both sides behave like gentlemen, and I would ask you to behave like a gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll take your instructions, of course. It is not my intention to behave on the other way. I'm just following the standards in common-law cross-examination, where the leading questions are allowed and where the control of the witness is of certain significance. That was my way how I posed the questions, and of course, Your Honour, it was not my intention to behave on the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, could you also check in your page 7. At the end of this page, you speak about 1997 figures, that give you some impression of the ethnic structure. Could you agree with me that, as a scientist, we -- or you should avoid impressions and you should rather speak about the facts and figures? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, you are not. I disagree, that here, using the expression "some impression" is wrong. I stressed in this way that the figures shown for two years, 1991 and, on the other hand, for 1997, are not fully comparable because of the difference in the age groups included in both cases. However, because the group of voters is so large that relative measures, as fractions, percentages, may be very well representative of the whole population, I still can put them together with the figures showing all age groups in the population. And this is even -- I didn't have to do this some impression, but I did it just to warn you that not to take these figures too literally. Further in the report I correct this inconsistency and I only show comparable, hundred per cent comparable figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My few last questions: How many years you are employed in Prosecution office?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Almost two years. Not yet two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You receive your salary from the Prosecution office. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I receive my salary from the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As a member of Prosecution office?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: As a member of the Prosecution office.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Madam Tabeau: You, as a scientist, why you mixed two methods, namely, I'm speaking about the OSCE voter register and statistic census 1991? I think that it's a kind of a mixing apples and oranges or, in our language, there is a saying that it's a mixture of grandmothers and frogs. So I think that you are a biased expert, that you are a one-sided expert, and that you didn't show a scientific approach to this report. Are you agree with me or not? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't agree, and I don't think that using the census, population census, together with voters register, is wrong. These are both individual level data sources and can be used in the same way. Matching is not a method I applied first in demography. Matching is a very well-established standard and has a long tradition, especially in Scandinavian countries, like Norway, for instance, or Finland. So I believe I properly used the same type of sources and well-established scientific standard as methods for producing this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've finished with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Ms. Tabeau. I will address you in my native language. As Mr. Pantelic said, I will put questions to you regarding your analysis of the pre-war municipality of Odzak and post-Dayton municipality of Odzak in the Federation, and Odzak-Vukosavlje. And then later on I will ask you a few general questions. So one question that will be a continuation of the few last questions put to you by Mr. Pantelic is this: Based on the methodology that you used, you, in fact, cannot tell us when, in the period between 1991 and 1997, these movements of the population in fact occurred. You were unable to establish that fact. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I didn't use any statistical information for the years between 1991 and 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First I would like you to take a look at the table 5. This pertains to Samac, but I think it is a good table to use for this question regarding the analysis that you used. So table 5A is the ethnic composition in Domaljevac, Samac, pre- and post-war population, residents 18 years or older. According to your table, in 1991 there were 26 Serb voters in Domaljevac-Samac municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In 1991, you mean? This is the number mentioned in the table. If it is a question related to age, I must tell you that we applied a cohort approach. So in this table, we, for the year 1991, showed the same cohort, the same group of people, who became eligible to vote in 1997. So it is not necessarily that this is the number, the 26, of all Serbs who were 18 and older in the year 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have established that six Serbs voted in 1997.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is what we see in the table, registered to vote in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what percentage of the total number of 27 is 6 voters?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So it would be a bit more than 2 per cent -- 20. A bit less than 20 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if 26 Serb voters lived there in 1991, and then in 1997 only 6 voters lived there, what percentage is that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Do you ask me questions now about the fractions that I included in the next columns of the table? So these fractions you can calculate in different ways. The fractions I showed in the table show the distribution, ethnic composition, for each year. It doesn't make any sense to relate the two numbers of Serbs to each other, because these numbers may not be related to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why cannot they be related to each other in order to establish what the reduction in percentages of the Serbs were? You have two identical categories of voters. You have voters in 1991 and then you have a category of voters in 1997. You made a comparison of the described categories and the voters, but now you are refusing to compare the amount of voters in 1991 and 1997. I'm asking you to please tell us what percentage of Serb voters remained in 1997 as compared to those in 1991. I'm not interested in the percentage of voters in relation to the entire population; I'm only interested in the population in relation to the Serb population.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I want to explain why these two numbers, 26 and 6, cannot be related to each other. The population of voters, 1997/1998 voters, as mentioned in the table, includes also Serb newcomers, so those Serbs who didn't live in this municipality in 1991. While 26 is only those who resided in this municipality in 1991. So it doesn't make much sense to compare two different figures. I could answer your question -- I can check how many of the 26 registered to vote, because they are included in the 6, and then I can show you, of course, what is this fraction. Of course, the numbers are very small, so I don't believe the fractions are really reliable because of the small sample size.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Shall we take our break now, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could just put a few more questions in order to close this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you are claiming that among those six, there were those Serbs who came to Domaljevac-Samac after 1991. Is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Possibly. Possibly. I would have to check this. But this is how the figures were produced. This is the fact of population in these two years. 1991 census is the resident population in this municipality, and 1997 is the population who registered to vote. And this is only part of this population in 1997 originally lived in this municipality in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can take our break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall continue at 1250 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Tabeau, we don't have much time left, and I will try to be as expeditious as possible so that we can finish today. So please refrain yourself to yes-or-no answers, if possible. If you need an explanation, then the Prosecution can do that during their re-direct. So, if you can, please follow my instructions. Now I will focus on Odzak municipality. I would like to remind you of what you said on page 16 of the English version of your report, namely, that in 1991, in municipality of Odzak - we're now talking about statistics - there were 10.056 residents. There were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the percentages of Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you speak slowly? The interpreters missed out the numbers. Perhaps you can repeat your numbers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So therefore, according to you, there were 30.056 residents, out of which, percentage-wise, 54.4 Croats, which is 16.338; 20.7 Muslims, which is 6.220; and 18.9 per cent of Serbs, or 5.667. So these are the official statistics that you used based on the 1991 census. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this applies to the entire municipality of Odzak?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, pre-war municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The pre-war municipality. Now, I have information, and it is similar to the equivalent of the information used by Mr. Pantelic. Based on the results of this census, before the war the municipality of Odzak, which, I have to say, is one of the municipalities with the largest number of economic immigrants, or people who went to work abroad in the former Yugoslavia. There were 4.923 residents working abroad at the time and that there were 1.559 members of their families. So by adding these two figures, I came to the number that a total number of residents from the municipality of Odzak working abroad in 1991 was 6.482, which is almost 25 per cent. And I would like to ask you, in relation to the answer you gave to Mr. Pantelic, the following: This number of 30.056 inhabitants which were found by the census of 1991 to be residents of the municipality of Odzak does not include those working abroad and members of their families; is that your claim?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is what I said is, in my opinion, the case. But again, I would need to look for statistics to check whether it is really the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to turn to the topic of Odzak itself. We will now first focus to Odzak in the Federation. On page 16 of the English version of your report, in paragraph 1, you come up with a conclusion that I would like to analyse now. In your last sentence, you stated that in the Odzak municipality, the fraction of Serbs remained more or less unchanged between 1991 and 1997. I would now like to turn to page 18 of your report, where you claim that, percentage-wise, in 1991, there were 22.6 per cent of Serbs eligible to vote in the territory covered by Odzak in the Federation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's the number in table 11A on page 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
