utterances.text: And that there were 28 Serbs who reported as voters and that there was 0.48 Serbs remaining -- percentage of Serbs remaining among the entire population. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is the same table. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, if we compare Muslims in the municipality of Samac, we conclude that there were many more Serbs than the Muslims in the municipality of Samac and that many more Serbs disappeared as compared to Muslims and Croats in the municipality of Samac. Am I right? I am deducing this based on the information that you provided.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are you now referring to Serbian part of municipality of Bosanski Samac? What -- I didn't get your point. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wish to make a comparison between the departure -- I would rather use that term than "dramatic decrease" in the Serbian population of Odzak municipality as compared to the disappearance or departure of the Muslim population in the municipality of Samac. There were more Serbs in Odzak than Muslims in Samac, based on your data, and more Serbs dramatically disappeared than Muslims in Odzak than Muslims in Samac. So am I right? I am quoting this from the information you provided.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I would like to be sure that we are referring to the same municipalities. We can speak about pre-war and post-war municipalities. So are you now referring to the pre-war or post-war municipalities? And if post-war, then which ones?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In pre-war municipality of Odzak, there were 3.000 Serb voters; is that right? Only 0.48 per cent of the entire population of them remained in the municipality of Odzak in 1997. This is your table 11A.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, the Federation, yes. That is correct. Yes, yes. And you compare this municipality with which municipality? RS? Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to compare your conclusion, which states that in Samac municipality - so another municipality - there was a dramatic decrease in the numbers of Muslims and Croats as compared to the pre-war municipality of Samac. You claim that in both of those municipalities there was a dramatic decrease: Serbs in Odzak and Muslims and Croats in Samac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't object to the question. I understand what my learned friend is driving at. But the witness hasn't said that. The witness was talking about the dramatic decrease in those numbers occurring in certain portions of the pre-war Bosanski Samac and Odzak municipalities. They were divided up. So the dramatic decrease that she talked about, for example, of Muslims and Croats from the Bosanski Samac area was from the Republika Srpska part of the Bosanski Samac -- of the former Bosanski Samac area. And that's -- my learned friend's question fails to take that into account. You see, she compared movement populations in four areas, not two; four. The two municipalities that have been split. And that's -- Mr. Lukic isn't taking that into account, with respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I wanted to be, and I was, fairly clear, but perhaps you are of a different view.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Was there a dramatic decrease of Serb population in Odzak municipality if we compare the pre-war and post-war municipality? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In the federal part of Odzak, yes, decrease of Serbs. In the federal part of Odzak municipality, we observed, after the war, compared with 1991, a dramatic decrease in the fraction of Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And based on your statistical view of ethnic cleansing, as you've told my colleague Pantelic, does that, if we take into account the short time period during which this population disappeared, does that, according to your standards which you used both for Muslims and Croats, represents, in statistical sense, a classical example of ethnic cleansing? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Because we used this term for a situation in which Muslims and Croats moved out or disappeared from a certain area. I think the same applies to the situation here, to be consequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you did not state so in your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Why don't you ask the crucial question: Why the Serb population in Odzak diminished in such a great number? This is the crucial question, not looking at the figures here on page 18, but for what reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I entirely agree with you, Your Honour Judge Lindholm, but I'm not sure that the witness will give us that kind of an answer. But I will put the question to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know why, what caused this dramatic decrease in the Serbian population in the municipality of Odzak as compared to the pre-Dayton population composition? Do you have any knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, this report and my testimony is about presenting a picture of changes, and not about explanation, so I, of course, cannot give this answer. I can only think that, again, such a rapid change cannot be caused by normal factors like demographic factors and socioeconomic factors, unless a crisis situation took place in this region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now that you have confirmed that we can use the term "ethnic cleansing," using the same standards for Serbs in Odzak, can you tell me why, on page 16, you claim that the fraction of Serbs in municipality of Odzak remained more or less unchanged between 1991 and 1997, if we can see that only 0.48 Serbs remained? Why did you come up with this conclusion on page 16 of your report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Because on page 16 I discuss the whole municipality of Odzak, without looking at the two parts of this municipality, federal and Serbian part of the municipality, and this is the reason why the figures that we present for the whole municipality must be different than the figures that are presented for certain smaller areas, parts of the municipalities. I said in the beginning of my testimony that the population was distributed within the pre-war municipalities very unequally, already in 1991, that certain ethnic groups were concentrated in certain areas. So if you look particularly at these areas where, for instance, Serbs were concentrated only, and other areas where only Croats were concentrated, then you obtain other fractions, other ethnic compositions. This is, I hope, understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are trying to say that these Serbs from Odzak, from the Federation, went on to live in Odzak-Vukosavlje, and that this is why the number of Serbs remained unchanged, more or less, in the entire municipality of Odzak. Is that what you're trying to tell us? Or perhaps they went somewhere outside the boundaries of the old Odzak municipality.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I'm not trying to say that these particular Serbs who lived in the federal part of Odzak municipality moved to the Serbian part of the municipality during the conflict. I can check this in my data. That is possible. I am trying to say - and I say it, I hope, very clearly - that there were population movements within the Odzak municipality, as there were between other municipalities, split in the Dayton Peace Accords. It is likely that many of them moved from the federal part to the RS part. It is likely. Certainly, it is. But we can check this even more thoroughly using results presented in this report by looking at figure --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which are on the table. Yes. We will come back to that when we examine Odzak-Vukosavlje. You are claiming that the fraction of Serbs remained more or less unchanged in the municipality of Odzak between 1991 and 1997. This is your conclusion on page 16, and this is what you are still upholding now. Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is true for the pre-war municipality of Odzak, but it is not true for the federal part of the municipality of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, we will now focus on the municipality of Odzak-Vukosavlje. You qualify this municipality as one in which there was significant ethnic cleansing. First I would like for us to look at the map in front of you, and tell us what constituted the municipality of Odzak pre-Dayton and what constitutes municipality of Vukosavlje post-Dayton. So the municipality of Odzak before Dayton, please, and now the municipality Odzak-Vukosavlje.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask you this: Are you quite sure, and are you claiming, that the pre-war Odzak was what you have just shown us, or was it perhaps a little bit smaller? Now I'm referring to the boundaries of the pre-war municipality of Odzak. Please try to recollect what you put in your report. On page 20, you go on to say that several settlements from Modrica were added onto the municipality of Odzak. Page 17, paragraph 4 in the English version. I will read it out now. This is what it says. You stated that several additional settlements, which in 1991 belonged to the neighbouring municipality of Modrica and Bosanski Samac, became part of the two new Odzak municipalities, according to the Dayton Agreement. Specifically, in 1995, Prud became part of the Federal Odzak, whereas Serb Odzak municipality received three settlements: Pecnik, Jakes, and Lug from Modricki, which, in 1991, were administrative part of Modrica. Can we please find these settlements on the map? They are quite easily discerned, near --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Near the municipal border. Pecnik and Jakes, yes, that's right. So we will agree, won't we, that before the conflict broke out or, rather, in 1991, these three settlements belonged to the municipality of Modica. This is what you said in your report. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is what I took from the OSCE classification scheme.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. Then you go on to say, on the same page, paragraph 4 in B/C/S version, that pre-war ethnic composition had 40 per cent of Croats and Muslims respectively and some 18 per cent of Serbs in this territory. As far as I understood it, this territory encompasses Dayton municipality Odzak-Vukosavlje, which had about 40 per cent Muslims, 40 per cent Croats, and about 17 or 18 per cent Serbs. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Approximately, the figures are correct. We are speaking about RS Vukosavlje. I want to note that the settlements that were under Modrica administration in 1991 are excluded from our analysis. So these fractions were obtained from data from which these settlements were excluded. We didn't increase our sample by including these settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Tabeau, that's not what you tell us in your report, and we will now be able to determine this based on your table. You did something completely opposite when you reached this conclusion that, in Vukosavlje municipality, there were 40 per cent Muslims and 40 per cent Croats. Namely, to the autonomous region of Odzak-Vukosavlje, you added 5.000 of residents from Modrica for the very simple reason of wanting to increase the number of Muslims and Croats. And I will prove this to you now. I'm using your data only, Ms. Tabeau. But first of all, let me ask you this, and this is something you already said to Mr. Pantelic, namely, that you have read the indictment. Have you read the indictment?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you have seen in the indictment that it covers, geographically, the municipalities of Bosanski Samac and Odzak from 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Then let's examine table 10, Odzak-Vukosavlje, where you claim -- and now I'm referring to percentages that you established based on the voters registration. You say that Odzak-Vukosavlje residents who lived in the pre-war municipality of Odzak, there were 2.050 residents. This is the sum of the first column. Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: That's the number that we see in the table, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you determined that, percentage-wise, in the pre-war settlements constituting Odzak municipality, which later belong to Odzak-Vukosavlje, there were 55.3 per cent Serbs, 0.3 per cent Muslims, or a total number of 7 Muslims; that there were 35.5 per cent Croats; and some 8.9 per cent of others. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. These are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you added to this residents of other villages, which are Gnojnica, the settlements that we just mentioned, Jakes, Modricka Lug, and Pecnik, and we -- you got a sum of 7.116 residents who are now currently living in Odzak or who then lived in the entire territory covered by today's Odzak-Vukosavlje. And then the population of Modrica was increased. In the population of Modrica, you increased the share of the Muslim population to 40, when before there were only 7, and I repeat, only 7 residents. So can you explain this? And let me add: 37.3 Croats and 4.5 per cent of others. Your conclusions are based on this data. We here - Trial Chamber, myself, and the Prosecution - are only interested in the pre-war municipality of Odzak. We are not interested in the residents of other municipalities that were added to this, other municipalities that have nothing to do with the indictment. My question is: The settlements that were included in the pre-war municipality of Odzak, were Serbs a majority there, with 55.3 per cent? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is probably you are right, that, by mistake, we indeed included all information, all records, also from the settlements, from Modrica. But I indeed must check the data and correct these tables and all related results. But it seems to me right now, when I compare these two figures from these two tables, that it was indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, Madam Tabeau, then we will draw another conclusion based on that. Your conclusion on page 24 of the English version, in which you say - your final conclusion - you claim that Muslims and Croats presented a considerable fraction of the actual population in the municipality Odzak-Vukosavlje before the war. Do you now agree with me that this cannot be true, that you cannot continue to uphold this? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Indeed, the composition now, I see, is different. The Croats are still represented considerably, but not Muslims, in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But Serbs were a majority population?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Seven Muslims, or 0.33 per cent, do not constitute considerable fraction of the population; yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another question that stems from this: Can you categorically claim, and can you agree with me, that perhaps these seven Muslims that before the war lived in Odzak-Vukosavlje municipality, who were voters, simply did not want to participate in the elections in 1997, did not want to report? Can we conclude this?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't know. Regarding the intentions of -- I don't know. I cannot comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were unable to establish this, and it is possible that a hundred per cent of Muslims are living today in Odzak-Vukosavlje municipality. It is quite possible. We cannot establish this. On page 8 -- on page 2 - I beg your pardon - you claim that Croats and Muslims were a dominant group in Odzak-Vukosavlje municipality. Is that right that this conclusion cannot be supported any more?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is all conditional on what you said, and I wrote in my report that these settlements that were from -- under Modrica administration, were indeed under Modrica administration in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, we read your report in its entirety, and we analysed it and we understood how you reached the conclusion and what data you used. But my question is as follows: In your conclusion, you say that in Odzak-Vukosavlje, before the war, in both of these areas, Croats and Muslims represented a considerable fraction of the actual population. Can you tell me now that Serbs and Croats, before the war, did not constitute a considerable fraction of the actual population? That's all I'm asking you now.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Croats indeed constituted a considerable fraction of the pre-war population in this municipality, in Odzak municipality, in both parts, but not the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But Serbs were dominant in Odzak-Vukosavlje municipality. Am I right or not?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... new fact. Serbs were dominant ethnic group in the Odzak-Vukosavlje Republika Srpska part of Odzak before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any re-examination, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, there is. Whether I can conclude today is another matter, of course, and that depends on the Chamber, but I'd like to go as far as I can, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just some features of your report, please. If you look at one of the maps that Mr. Pantelic showed you, page 30 -- I apologise. I think it was page 27. You were being asked questions as to the -- whether the Dayton line basically followed the ethnic outlines that you can see on that map in the bottom part of the page. You agreed. The red sways that you can see on the map there in fact merely show areas where Serbs were greater than 50 per cent of the population; therefore, there could be situations in which there were significant proportions of non-Serbs living in those red areas, up to 49 per cent. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Is that question to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So the red areas are where Serb population was in absolute majority, 50 per cent or more?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right. But in those red areas, of course, there could be very significant numbers of non-Serbs living, up to 49 per cent.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You were asked questions about your expertise by Mr. Pantelic. You were asked questions regarding whether you had dealt with demographic issues prior to your work here at the Office of the Prosecutor, and you established that you had indeed done work on mortality issues and not census issues. Can you tell us when you gained your expertise in demographics and whether or not that included the gaining of any expertise on the use of censuses in studying demographics.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I studied statistics and econometrics, and graduated in statistics and econometrics. As part of the courses at my university, I followed a course in demography, including, of course, population surveys and censuses, with an extensive empirical part as part of this course. Later, I worked at a university where I taught statistics and descriptive statistics, mathematical statistics, demographic forecasting, these type of issues. I did my Ph.D. in mathematical demography, and throughout my thesis about regional mortality differences in Poland, in the 1980s. I also proposed an explanation to these differences. Later I moved from Poland to the Netherlands, and last ten years -- not last ten years, but I worked ten years in the Dutch National Institute of Demography. In this institute, I was responsible, as a senior researcher and project leader, for conducting projects and proposing new projects in the area of mortality forecasting, but I also have done some work related to population forecasting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We have that in report. I mean, we have running out of time. We have all this data in her report. This is my objection. We have in the report. And this is not a crucial moment for the re-direct. And then we shall be in problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you want me to reply to that, if Your Honours -- well, it was a topic raised by my learned friend. He was the one who raised the issue with the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- regarding her expertise in censuses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but it's contained in her C.V., isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because you could have just referred her C.V. to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, it is contained. I assumed, therefore, that Mr. Pantelic had read it before he even asked the question, but perhaps I'll leave it and move on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The census in 1991 that was conducted in Bosnia and Herzegovina, did it distinguish between people who were actually resident in Bosnia and Herzegovina and people who were working overseas?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In my view, the census covered the population who resided at the moment of the census in the country, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and those who resided abroad were actually not reported in the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's your reason for saying that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, we have some materials, instructions, for instance, for the interviewers, and legal grounds for the census, in which this type of guidelines are included, and of course we studied these guidelines before we started to analyse this data.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Therefore, based on the guidelines that you're aware of, the census was not recording people who lived and worked overseas, or out of the country?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, you refer throughout to split settlements. Can you explain to the Chamber what exactly you mean by "split settlements"?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Split settlements are small geographic areas located very -- in a very close neighbourhood of the Dayton line, and in these settlements, one part of the settlement belongs to one political entity and the other part to the other political entity. It is possible to distinguish who is living where, who is residing where, only on the basis of the addresses of the population living in these settlements. We didn't have any official classification schemes that would include addresses that we could then use to regroup individuals to either municipality. So this is why, taking the conservative approach, not to increase any statistics, we excluded all split settlements from our analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Putting it very crudely -- tell me if I'm right or wrong, please, but putting it very crudely, is this the case: Some of the split settlements of towns or villages that have got a line drawn through them, that's basically the Dayton line, people might claim to come from the town, but when they do, you can't tell which side of the line they're living on because they don't give you --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No. I think, in reality, it is clear where they live, whether in federal or RS part of the pre-war municipality of Odzak or Bosanski Samac. I'm speaking about statistical definition of the place of residence. In order to be able to statistically distinguish between different municipalities, one belonging to the Federation, one belonging to the Republika Srpska, I need a guide with addresses that I could use to regroup individuals. So it is not that in reality it is unknown, unclear, where the people live in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Why did you exclude them from your consideration?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, because I didn't have such guidelines. I didn't have any knowledge that I could use to include these records in my analysis. This is why.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did, in your opinion, your decision to excluded them from your consideration have a general impact on the general conclusions that you reached?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I believe not, because we looked carefully at the sample size in each particular municipality analysed in this report, and the sample sizes were big enough to produce statistics, especially relative measures, like fractions, percentages, and to discuss them in that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's look at the last issue raised by Mr. Lukic, the very last issue, a few moments ago, regarding your conclusions about the population in the Republika Srpska part of Odzak. Did you take into account a number of -- in looking at that part of the former municipality of Odzak, a number of towns that had formerly been part of Modrica?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Three settlements, three small settlements, well, were not apparently part of Odzak municipality before the war, but this had been the case -- had become the case after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. I see.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: And actually, my intention was not to include these settlements but exclude them from the analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Now, do you have any idea of the sort of numbers that we're talking about as far as those three settlements are concerned?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think I know. It is mentioned in the table that Mr. Lukic discussed with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where? Can you show us in the report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is on page 17 in my English version of the report, table 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So the difference, if we look at the total given for Odzak-Vukosavlje, we have two total numbers. One number is 2.050, reconstructed from the pre-war Odzak, and the second number, all components, is 7.116.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. And --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So the difference would be related to the settlements, new settlements, that were under Modrica administration, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And is the inclusion of those three settlements in your calculations likely to have pumped up, increased, the figure that we can see of 7.116?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think the most important consequence of including these figures is that the Serb population shown in our report is not in majority in the Serb part of Odzak in 1991. And, in fact, if we would exclude these settlements, Serb population would become a majority, in 1991. So it would be a municipality that would have an absolute majority of Serb population before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. That means greater 50 per cent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, greater 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But still, we would have 35.5 per cent Croats in this municipality, which is a very considerable minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. How long and how easily -- let me withdraw that question and start again. If you had to recalculate those figures, excluding the figures that you wrongly took into account from the three settlements of Modrica, how long would it take you to do that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think that we could do it immediately, and, well, I understand that Monday is the next session of this Court. Then we could present new figures by Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have those figures by Monday, and figures not including the three settlements that were wrongly included?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. The only thing is will be -- would be then corrected and adjusted by excluding the three settlements from Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I seek an adjournment at this stage. It's almost 1.45, and I seek an adjournment so that the witness can complete that task that I've just directed her attention to. If you want to get the full benefit of her evidence, in my submission, it would be time well spent and would enable her to present a more accurate picture to the Tribunal -- to the Chamber, and I could finish her evidence briefly, my re-examination, on that occasion. And if she were to prepare a small extra report, I could provide it to my learned friends so that they're not prejudiced, and of course I would have no objection to any further re-examination by them on that, if you were to grant me my application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is using the same figures that are already contained in the report, excluding those settlements which she described having been included?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's just basically relooking at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Revising.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Revising.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One table.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Revising one table, the Serb part of the former Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I address the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber wanted to find out from the Defence -- because all the witness would be doing is to revise this table by deducting the population from those settlements which were wrongly included. The Trial Chamber wanted to find out whether the Defence would want to raise questions with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour -- yes, I will be very brief. First of all, this report could be done -- it's just minor changes, although we could do that immediately. I mean, everyone can deduct these figures. But for the sake of fairness, we do not object that this witness will prepare a report, revised version of this table, and submit by Monday. But, Your Honour, we strongly and firmly object to any further re-examination of the Prosecution of this witness because, point 1: My learned friend informed this Trial Chamber that this witness, Madam Tabeau, will not be able here in the Hague until September, and we designated today a day for this chief and cross-examination. Point 2: This witness just said to us - and it's on the transcript - that actually, she will be here on Monday. Point 3: We prepared our cross-examination in view of these time limits for one day, and therefore, we think, and we strongly oppose, and we respectfully move this Trial Chamber to preclude the Prosecution for further examination in re-direct. Should that be the case - I don't know how and when - then the Defence reserve its right for expand the time for our initial cross-examination. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only a second or two, Your Honours, because this topic has to do with my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you wait?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My explanation, Your Honours, would be the following, since this is the topic that I covered in my cross-examination: I cross-examined -- and the witness can confirm this on the basis of the data contained in her statement. All the questions raised by my learned friend are contained in the statement. Perhaps we were reading these statements, and that made everything more complex and complicated, but everything that has to do with the Odzak-Vukosavlje municipality is contained in this report. I don't know why this has to be repeated. The figures that have to do with 1991 are contained in the first column, and they were confirmed by the witness. One thing. Another thing, Your Honours: We really coordinated our cross-examination given the limitation of the time available today. First, the learned friend said that it would only take him a few minutes for the direct, and it took us much longer. I abbreviated my cross so that we can complete today, and I really strongly object to this situation in which, in the re-direct, new topics are being raised. My only reason to reduce the number of my questions by about 30 - and Mr. Pantelic says that I tried to cover the general topics - was done for the sole purpose of finishing the cross with this witness. And everything that I raised can be confirmed by the witness, either orally or the witness can do it later in writing, but we certainly strongly object to any additional re-direct of this witness on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has decided that the witness can revise the table in question and sign her revised report and file it. There will be no further re-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. So -- fine. So I just want to be clear so that everything is done properly and so the witness is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What the Chamber is saying is that she will go back, prepare another written report, or brief report, or summary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, to correct this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- correcting the table, explaining why she has corrected it and how she has corrected it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- any conclusions that she draws from that, and we would -- she would then provide it to the Prosecution, it will be filed, that's the end of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. I understand. Thank you very much. I have nothing further to say on the topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until Monday. Oh, I see. Yes. I forgot to release the witness. Thank you very much, Ms. Tabeau, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. You are now free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Starting from Monday, we are sitting in the afternoon because of the video conference. We hope it will take place. So we will start at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this has nothing to do with the witness, but it is indeed of crucial importance that the Trial Chamber be informed about a very important fact that has to do with our clients. We would need only one or two minutes to clarify this issue, which has to do with the status of our clients in the prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why can't it be done in writing? Because we are delaying the afternoon session, as you know. We can deal with it on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, our clients, yesterday, in the afternoon, were told that tomorrow, on Thursday, they would be transferred, and I am speaking on behalf of Zaric and Tadic, that they would be transferred to another building of the detention facility. We are concerned that should we fail to inform the Trial Chamber about this fact today -- I apologise for doing it now. This hasn't got anything to do with the direct trial procedure, but it has to do with the rights of the clients. Our clients Tadic and Zaric are very much concerned with the fact that they will now be transferred from one detention facility to another. They were told that this would happen tomorrow, and they were told yesterday. And in this stage of the trial, it is indeed very difficult for them to change the environment. This is a very important fact which might be considered by some as a technical detail only, but our clients are afraid that in this stage of the trial they would psychologically find it very distressing. When we learned about this fact, we tried to establish contact with the detention facility management. We will try to do it this afternoon. However, the clients asked us to address the Trial Chamber, to inform the Trial Chamber about this fact, and we would certainly not want, in this stage of the trial, to deteriorate their situation. They have been in this facility for quite some time. They got accommodated with the facilities, and they would find it very difficult indeed to be transferred to another environment. You can imagine yourselves what the situation would be if they had to adapt in the middle of the trial to another environment. Of course, I personally will also contact the detention facility management, but I wanted to inform the Trial Chamber, and I apologise for taking all this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. The Trial Chamber will respond in writing, since we are not sitting tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1.52 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
